rumours: Justiciars walked a man out of the Elven Gardens in irons last Loredas. A Talos amulet sewn into his coat lining, they say. His wife still lays a place for him at supper.
Kvatch has walls again. Not a whole city, mind, but walls, with the Count's banner on them for the first time since the Gates. Savlian Matius says the rest will take a generation.
The Gold Road toll went up two drakes at Skingrad. The Count says it pays for bridges. I've walked that road twice this month and I've yet to see a new bridge.
Half of Cheydinhal speaks Dunmeri now. Ever since the mountain burst, the refugees kept coming over the Valus passes, and they never stopped coming.
Bravil's watch found another skooma boat under the bridge, loaded to the gunwales with Senchal sugar. The Khajiit on the docks swear they've never seen it before in their lives.
The old Daedric shrines out in the wilds have been busy since the war. More smoke, more offerings. When the Nine go quiet, folk start knocking on other doors.
Bruma sells iron north over the mountains and calls it trade with kin. The Legion pretends not to notice, so long as the Stormcloaks keep their quarrel on their own side of the Jeralls.
legends: When the Gates opened, two hundred years gone, the sky over Kvatch burned for a night and a day. Gold Coast farmers still won't plough the hill where the first Gate stood. Whatever grows there, they say, comes up the colour of rust and tastes of ash.

Before men, the Heartland belonged to the Ayleids, who built in white stone and kept captive stars in glass. Their welkynd stones still glow in the ruins. A farmer who carries one home will find his milk soured and his dog barking at the cellar door, until he carries it back.

In the Temple District stands a dragon of stone, caught mid-roar over the ruin of the old Temple of the One. The priests say the last of the Septims became that dragon. Children are told that if they lay a hand on its claw and tell the truth, it is warm; if they lie, it is cold as a grave.

songs.title: The Red Ring
lines: Round the White-Gold the Elves made a ring,
Steel on the water and fire on the wing,
Twelve thousand fell where the Rumare runs red,
And the Emperor rode with the living and dead.
Drink to the Ring, lads, and drink to the cost,
And never ask after the treaty we lost.

songs.title: Gold Road Wagoner
lines: Up from Kvatch with a load of stone,
Down from Skingrad with wine for home,
Mind the bandit and mind the toll,
And the Gold Road will take its share of your soul.

rumours: The Arena's got a new Grand Champion every other season since the war. Fixed fights, they say. The Blue Team's bettors drink at the Waterfront and they're never short of coin.
There's lights at the old shrine of Meridia north-east of the city again, and not the good kind. A shepherd saw bones walking in a line, like pilgrims.
The Thalmor Embassy took another house on the Talos Plaza. Nobody sold it to them. The family just isn't there anymore.
The Rumare's full of eels this year. My father says that means a hard winter; my mother says it means my father should mend the nets instead of talking.
legends: The White-Gold Tower was raised by the Ayleids around a stone that sings. Every hundred years, on a still night, the Tower hums a single note, and every glass in the city rings in answer. The last time, folk say, was the night before the Elves came over the walls.

rumours: A woodcutter out of Bruma went up the north trail for pine and came back without his axe, his boots or his voice. He writes on slates now. He writes the same word over and over: 'chains'.
There's a ring of fighters at the old Boethiah stones south-west of town. Sell-swords from both sides of the border, cutting each other for coin and for a Prince who keeps no score.
The Pale Pass is open early this year. Nords coming down, Nords going up, and every second wagon has a false bottom.
Snow-trolls took two goats off the Hrodmund place. The Count's huntsmen are 'considering the matter'. Meanwhile we eat porridge.
legends: When the Gate opened outside Bruma in the Crisis, the Nords of the town sang the old war songs so loud that the dremora at the gate faltered. The town still sings them every Frostfall, on the night of the battle, and no one in Bruma is ever allowed to stop mid-verse.

songs.title: Bruma Gate
lines: Stone at our backs and the snow at our feet,
The sky burning red and no road for retreat,
We sang till the mountains sang with us again,
And the gate fell silent, and so did the men.

rumours: The Great Oak in Chorrol dropped a branch the size of a cart on the chapel steps. The priests call it an omen. The carpenters call it firewood.
There's a fellow in Chorrol, Ostorius Varro, who was drowning in debt last spring. Now he's dry and every one of his creditors is dead. Ask him how and he goes white.
The Fighters Guild posted a bounty on goblins in the hills west of town. Twenty drakes an ear. My cousin's been sharpening his knife and practising his growl.
The beggars of Chorrol walk south to the old Namira stones every new moon and come back fat. Nobody asks what they eat out there. Nobody wants to know.
legends: The Colovian horse-lords swore oaths on their swords, never on gods, because gods change their minds and steel doesn't. That's why a Colovian's handshake is worth more than a Nibenese contract, and why Colovians are so bad at contracts.

rumours: Cheydinhal's Dunmer have opened a third shrine to the Tribunal in the old Imperial chapel cellar. The Count pretends it's a wine store.
A Mages Guild scholar went up to the Hermaeus Mora stones north of the city with forty books and a mule. The mule came back.
Don't buy a house in Cheydinhal that's going cheap. My brother-in-law did, and he's never got the smell out of the cellar.
Thieves in the Nibenay pray to Nocturnal at the stones west of Cheydinhal before a big job. If the night is moonless they take it as a yes.
legends: The Nibenese say every river in the Basin is a strand of a single net cast by the Divines to hold the Heartland together. Where a strand is cut, by a dam or a bridge built without a priest, the land on either side quarrels for a hundred years.

rumours: The Count of Skingrad's never seen at noon. Never. My grandfather says he wasn't seen at noon in his grandfather's day either.
There's a revel in the hills between Skingrad and Kvatch where the wine never runs out and the guests never leave. A vintner's daughter went last month. She's still dancing, they say.
Hunters out of Skingrad won't shoot a white stag in the Weald. Last fellow who did woke with the antlers on his pillow and the stag nowhere in sight.
Tomato blight's in the lower vineyards and a cough's going through the farms by the Peryite shrine. Same week, same farms. You don't need a priest to add that up.
legends: The first vine of the West Weald was planted by a Colovian soldier who swore he'd never shed blood again. He made wine instead of war, and the Weald grapes are red because they drink what he gave up. Skingrad vintners still pour the first cup of every barrel onto the soil.

songs.title: The Two Barrels
lines: One for the Count and one for the cellar,
One for the stranger and one for the teller,
Drink up the Shiraz and drink up the Tamika,
And thank the Nine there's no Skingrad seeker.

rumours: The East Empire Company has three new ships in Anvil harbour and not one sailor willing to crew them for Company wages. They're hiring Khajiit and Redguards off the docks and paying in promises.
Kvatch's masons are mostly Orcs now, hired out of the Valus. They do good work and they hold a grudge for a hundred years if you shortchange them.
Pirates off the Abecean have a new captain. They say she spares any ship that flies a Kvatch flag. Nobody knows why, which makes it worse.
A boy digging in the Kvatch rubble found a Count's seal-ring. The steward took it off him and gave him a single drake. That's Gold Coast justice for you.
legends: Anvil's lighthouse was lit once by a woman whose husband never came back from the Abecean. She kept it burning forty years, and when she died the lamp went out on its own. The keepers say it gutters, still, whenever a widow climbs the stairs.

rumours: The Lucky Old Lady in Bravil turned her face a finger's breadth east in the night. Every skooma-boatman on the river's laying bets on what it means.
Hooded folk camp by the old Dagon shrine west of town. The watch counted nine of them. The Imperial Cult wants a sword sent; the watch wants a raise first.
The Mad God's shrine north-west of Bravil has a new offering bowl. It's a soup tureen. It's full of buttons. Nobody admits to the buttons.
A dream-seller in the Bravil slums sells sleep by the hour. You lie in her loft and wake with somebody else's memories. Half the beggars in town are hooked on it.
legends: Bravil was built where the Niben drowns its secrets. Every flood leaves something on the bank: a ring, a door, once a whole boat with the table laid for supper. The Bravilese throw back anything they can't explain, and they can't explain most things.

rumours: Leyawiin's Count has doubled the guard on the river gate since the Argonians took back Blackwood's south bank in the last age. They never forgave and we never forgot.
A noblewoman of Leyawiin buried her third husband this spring. Lovely funeral. She wore Mephala's black, which some folk thought a peculiar choice.
The marsh between Leyawiin and the Vaermina stones is full of sleepers. Folk who lay down to rest in the reeds and won't wake. Their eyes move under the lids.
Fighters Guild lads are pulling mudcrabs as big as cartwheels out of the Blackwood flats. Good eating if you can get the shell off before it gets your hand.
legends: The Blackwood is so named because the trees drink so much black water their heartwood turns dark as ebony. Carpenters who use it say the boards creak at night in a language nobody in Leyawiin speaks, but every Argonian in Leyawiin pretends not to understand.

rumours: Ash came down on Mournhold three days running, all the way across the Inner Sea. Old folk put out bowls of water for the ancestors, so they'd have something clean to drink.
The Archcanon calls on the Great Houses to stand together. The Houses agree, and then they go home and count each other's guards.
Argonian raiders crossed the Deshaan border again last month. Burned a kwama egg farm and wrote something in the ash with their claws. Nobody will say what it said.
A Telvanni wizard grew a tower overnight on the coast past Sadrith Mora. The tower next door woke up, so they say, and it was not pleased.
Sleepers are walking out of the ash in Balmora and Ald'ruhn again. Not many. Enough. The Temple calls it a sickness. My grandmother calls it a memory.
Necrom's had so many pilgrims since the Red Year that the dead are complaining about the noise. The priests swear it's true. The priests would know.
legends: When the moon that Vivec held in the sky came down in the Red Year, it did not fall like a stone. It fell slowly, like a held breath let go, and those who saw it say it wept fire the whole way down. Some Dunmer still will not look at the sky on the anniversary.

Azura told the Chimer they would be changed, and they were: grey-skinned and red-eyed, the colour of ash and blood. The Ashlanders say this was not a curse but a reminder. A people who betray their hero should wear the colour of what that betrayal costs.

The Daedra whom the Dunmer call the House of Troubles stand at the four corners of the land like posts of a tent: Molag Bal, Malacath, Sheogorath, Mehrunes Dagon. Pull one post, and the tent sags. Pull all four and the sky falls in. So the Temple does not destroy their shrines. It watches them.

songs.title: Ash-Yam Song
lines: Dig the yam and shake the ash,
Mind the guar and mind the lash,
Mountain sleeps and mountain wakes,
Mountain gives and mountain takes.
Sing it low and sing it slow,
The ancestors are listening below.

songs.title: The Moon Came Down
lines: The moon came down on Vivec's town,
And the sea came up to meet it,
We lost our god and kept our gods,
And the Houses still compete it.

rumours: The Twilight Stone was stolen from Azura's shrine east of Mournhold by Argonian raiders, forty-three winters gone. Priestess Ilvari has been looking for it her whole life.
A Meridian zealot smashed the ancestor shrine of House Llethan's cousins near the Meridia stones. Called the bones an abomination. The family has posted a reward for his ears.
Mournhold's Great Bazaar has Argonian goods again, sold by Hlaalu factors who swear they came by way of Cyrodiil. They didn't.
The Orcs who work the Ebonheart docks go up to the Malacath stones on feast days. The Ordinators follow them. Nobody's come to blows yet.
legends: Mournhold was built where Almalexia first set her foot in the Deshaan, and for an age the city glowed at night from within. When she was gone, the glow went out house by house over a single winter. The last house to go dark is said to be the one where the city's first mason was born.

rumours: The plantations along the Ascadian coast pay their field hands in coin now, by Imperial law. They pay in coin and charge for the roof. The sums come out much the same.
Somebody left a fresh heart at the Molag Bal stones between Balmora and Vivec. Not an animal heart, the Ordinators say. They're asking questions in every canton.
The Hlaalu councillors pray at the Boethiah stones before every council vote. Never together. Never on the same night.
legends: Vivec raised his city on the water so that no army could march on it, only sail, and no fleet could take it, because the cantons themselves would close their doors and float. Nobody has ever seen a canton float. Everyone in Vivec has an uncle who has.

rumours: The Camonna Tong own every second door in Balmora. If an Imperial asks you for directions, give him the wrong ones. Safer for everyone.
A Caldera ebony miner wished at the Clavicus stones for a vein that would never run out. It hasn't. He's still down there digging, and he won't come up to eat.
Fevyn Andalor's brother walks out of Balmora in his sleep every night, always north-east, always toward the mountain. She ties him to the bed now. He chews through the rope.
legends: The Odai river was cut by a single tear Vivec shed for the Chimer who died at Red Mountain. The water is sweet because grief, the Hlaalu say, is the one thing that never goes sour.

rumours: Ash storm on the way to Ald'ruhn. Seal your doors, cover your guar, and if somebody knocks in the storm, don't open. Nobody knocks in a storm.

A Telvanni mouth was seen at the Hermaeus Mora stones west of Ald'ruhn, bargaining with something in the rock. The Redoran guard sent word to the Temple and then to the mouth's master. Only one answered.
Bal Molagmer are back, they say. Thieves who only rob those who've wronged the poor. Ald'ruhn's councillors have started locking their doors twice.
legends: Ald'ruhn is built inside the shell of an emperor crab so large that it took a hundred Redoran warriors a hundred days to kill it. The shell still hums in an ash storm. Children are told it is the crab, dreaming of the sea.

rumours: Sadrith Mora's guard asks your business at the dock. Say 'trade'. Never say 'study'. A Telvanni hears 'study' and wonders whose secrets you're after.
Mistress Dratha's tower has been coughing up spores for a week. The fishers say she's sneezing. Nobody in Sadrith Mora finds that funny.
A Telvanni hireling contract was read out in the Gateway Inn, all forty clauses. The man who signed it is now a mushroom. Read before you sign.
legends: The first Telvanni tower was grown from a spore a wizard carried in his mouth across the sea, because he trusted no pocket. When he spat it onto the shore, it rooted before it touched the sand, and it has been growing upward and arguing ever since.

rumours: The East Empire Company is losing money at Ebonheart and everyone in the Company knows except the Factor. He still thinks it's the weather.
The Legion garrison at Ebonheart is half the size it was before the Great War. The other half went to Cyrodiil and never came back. The Argonians have noticed.
Kwama miners near Ebonheart broke into an old Daedric cellar. They sealed it again the same day. Nobody will say what was down there, but they're drinking more.
legends: Ebonheart was built from the black stone of the Stonefalls, which fell from the sky when Lorkhan's heart was torn out. Masons say the stone is still warm in the middle, and that if you lay your ear to the castle wall at night you can hear something counting.

rumours: Necrom's priests are asking for help in the City of the Dead. Grave-robbers broke a dozen urns last month and carried off the ashes for some Daedric rite.
Red-robed worshippers at the Dagon stones west of Necrom. The Ordinators went in five strong and came back four. The Temple's quiet about the fifth.
The pilgrims to Necrom say the Mad God's shrine on the road talks to you if you walk past it alone. It asks after your mother. It knows her name.
legends: Necrom is the oldest city of the dead in Morrowind. Every Dunmer family wishes to rest there, and the dead are packed so close beneath the streets that the priests say a funeral is really a negotiation: the new arrival must be introduced, and the old ones must agree to move up.

rumours: The Ghostfence still holds, the Temple says. The Temple also said the moon would never fall.
The Morag Tong walk up to the Mephala stones under the mountain's shoulder. They say there are spiders nesting there now, big as netch.
Ash pilgrims climb the mountain every Mid Year and leave bowls of water at the crater's lip. Most of them come back down. Most.
legends: Red Mountain is the Heart's grave, the Ashlanders say. Lorkhan's heart was hidden beneath it, and every Dunmer feels it beat at least once in their life, usually on the night before something terrible.

rumours: The King's envoy in Stormhold signs contracts with a claw-mark now, not a seal. The Imperials left their seals behind when they left. The Saxhleel left them in the mud.
There's sickness in the roots of the great Hist, they say. The sap-thieves are bleeding the trees while they're weak. Everybody's angry and nobody can say at whom.
Dunmer slavers haven't dared the border in forty years, but something's been taking Saxhleel off the Shadowfen paths. Somebody's chains have come back.
Imperial plantations round Gideon stand empty, half of them. Vines through the windows. The Lukiul who stayed say the houses sigh at night for their old masters. Good, say the others.
A skooma barge from Senchal ran aground off Lilmoth. The whole harbour was singing for three days. The King has asked very politely that it not happen again.
The old Daedric stones in the Shadowfen were built by Dunmer, Imperials, Kothringi, nobody remembers. The Saxhleel let them stand. The Hist didn't object, so neither do we.
legends: The Hist were here before the land. They dreamed the marsh and then they dreamed the Saxhleel to walk in it. When an Argonian dies, the Hist remembers them, and if you lay your cheek against the bark of your egg-tree on a still night, you can hear your grandmother's voice, faint, in the sap.

Before the Saxhleel, the Kothringi lived in the marsh, silver-skinned folk who traded with everyone. Then came the Knahaten Flu, and in a single season they were gone, every one. The Saxhleel did not catch it. Nobody has ever proven why. Some Imperials still say the Hist did it on purpose. The Hist does not answer.

The Shadowscales are hatched under the moonless sign of the Shadow and given to the Sithis of the marsh to raise. A mother who gives up a Shadowscale egg weeps for one night only, and then never speaks of it again, and the whole village honours her silence.

songs.title: Root and Water
lines: Root in the water, water in the root,
Egg in the mud and the mud in the fruit,
We were here before the Empire, we'll be here when it's gone,
The Hist remembers everyone, and the marsh goes on.

rumours: Stormhold's still half Imperial stone and half Saxhleel reed. The Lukiul who keep the old customs-house still write their ledgers in Cyrodilic, out of habit, and the young ones mock them for it.

Five Daedric shrines in a row in the marsh west of Stormhold, close as beads on a string. The elders say an Imperial governor built them, one a year, trying to find a Prince who'd keep him alive in the swamp. None did.
A Gideon scholar went to read at the Hermaeus Mora stones west of town. Her assistant came back alone and wouldn't stop counting his fingers.
The Shadowscales are hiring again. Not hiring. Choosing. Same thing, if they choose you.
legends: Stormhold was a Saxhleel town before the Imperials built their walls around it, and it will be a Saxhleel town when the walls are moss. The elders say that when the Imperial governor raised his flag over the gate, the river rose and drowned the flagpole up to the eagle's neck, and left it there.

rumours: The plantation houses round Gideon are being stripped for stone. The Saxhleel take the walls and leave the ballrooms open to the rain. Lovely in a storm, I hear.
An Imperial magistrate near Gideon still keeps Saxhleel in 'debt-service'. The King has noticed. People who are noticed by the King don't stay noticed for long.
The Mages Guild in Gideon lost a scholar to the marsh. Lirrian, a Breton. Went out to read with the Hist and the Daedra and came back... well, she didn't.
legends: Gideon was where an Imperial empress was born, they say, a girl of Black Marsh who went to the White-Gold Tower. The Imperials built her a statue in the square. The Saxhleel tell a different story: that she went north because the Hist told her to, and that she never stopped hearing its voice in the Tower.

rumours: Helstrom's closest to the Dunmer border and the most nervous for it. When the wind blows from the north the Saxhleel smell ash and the old ones start sharpening their spears.
There are Morag Tong in the marsh near Helstrom. They walk like they own the paths. The Shadowscales are not pleased.
The shrines of the Dunmer's House of Troubles stand just north of Helstrom, right on the border. Raiders from both sides camp near them, because nobody honest goes there.
legends: When the Saxhleel marched north into Morrowind in the Red Year's wake, the warriors of Helstrom were first across the border. They came back carrying nothing but the chains their grandparents had worn, and they sank them in the black pool at the edge of town. The pool has never been clear since.

rumours: Lilmoth's harbour is full of ships from everywhere. Khajiit from Senchal, Redguards, even a Thalmor cutter, which nobody here invited and nobody here will sell water to.
The old Imperial customs house in Lilmoth sank into the harbour mud when the Empire left. The customs-master's strongbox went with it, so they say, full of every bribe paid in thirty years.
The King of Argonia holds court in Lilmoth with no crown, no throne and no guards that you can see. You can't see the Shadowscales either. That's rather the point.
legends: Lilmoth was drowned once, in the age of the Kothringi, and raised again by the Hist in a single night. The fishers say that on the lowest tide of the year you can still see the old Kothringi rooftops below the harbour, silver as their makers, and lights moving in the windows.

rumours: Somebody's been stealing hatchling eggs from Murkmire and selling them to Imperial collectors. The Egg-Keeper's posted guards. The guards are her grandsons. They're very serious about it.
Murkmire's the deep marsh. Paths move. Trees walk. If a Saxhleel offers to guide you, pay what they ask and don't argue.
Archeins and Bright-Throats are feuding again in the Murkmire villages. Over a stolen canoe, this time. Last time it was a song.
legends: In Murkmire they say the Hist of each village chooses one hatchling in a generation to carry the village's whole memory. That child never learns to read and never needs to. Ask them anything about the village's past and they will answer in the voice of whoever was there.

rumours: The Shadowfen's stitched with Daedric shrines along the Morrowind border. Dunmer raised some, Imperials raised others. The Saxhleel just call them 'the noisy stones'.
Rot-eaters at the Namira stones south of Mournhold have a pale stone that glows at dusk. They light their feasts by it. It was stolen from the Dunmer, they say. They say it like a joke.
Somebody's taking Saxhleel off the Shadowfen paths and chaining them at the Molag Bal stones near the Necrom border. Somebody who speaks Dunmeri and wears a Hlervu ring.
legends: The Shadowfen is where the Knahaten Flu first rose, the elders say, from a pool that no Saxhleel will drink from. The Kothringi drank from it. The pool is still there, still clear and sweet, and the herons won't land on it.

rumours: The Mane receives the Thalmor envoys in Riverhold with every courtesy and sends them home with nothing. This one thinks the Mane has been doing it for forty years and is very good at it.
Moon sugar is dear this season. The Moon-Bishop says the fields are being raided. The skooma-cooks say the Moon-Bishop is raising prices. Both are probably telling the truth, which is very annoying.
The Renrijra Krin laugh in the dunes outside Rimmen and steal from Thalmor wagons. The Thalmor call them bandits. Many Khajiit call them cousins. A few call them dinner guests.
A caravan stopped for water at the Peryite stones south of Rimmen and came to Torval with half its people coughing and walking in straight lines. Ri'jasha the caravaneer is looking for a brave fool.
The Elves say they saved the moons. In the Void Nights, the moons went dark, and the Thalmor brought them back, and they never, ever let the Khajiit forget it.
Senchal's harbour has more skooma in it than water, the sailors say. That's a lie, of course. It's about even.
legends: Azurah made the Khajiit from the Bosmer who lived in Elsweyr, shaping each kind by the phase of the moons on the night it was born: the great Senche, the swift Cathay, the small and clever Ohmes. That is why a Khajiit's form is a matter of the sky, and why every Khajiit mother watches the moons on the night her cubs come.

The Lunar Lattice is the road the moons walk, and the Khajiit are its keepers. When the moons went dark in the Void Nights, the Moon-Priests did not run. They sat in the temples and sang to the empty sky every night for two years, and when the moons came back, the first thing they saw was a Khajiit still singing.

Namiira is the Great Darkness, the first thing, older than the Lattice. Khajiit whose souls fall into her when they die become Dro-m'Athra, the dark-souled, who hunger for the moons' light because they can no longer find it. That is why Khajiit leave a candle burning for the newly dead, so that they can see the way home.

songs.title: Two Moons Dancing
lines: Masser is the elder and Secunda is the small,
Masser takes the long way and Secunda takes it all,
Dance them on the Lattice, dance them through the sand,
And one day they will dance you home, with sugar in your hand.

songs.title: The Caravan Song
lines: Up from Senchal, down from Rimmen,
Twelve good wagons and one bad cousin,
Sugar for the Bishop and silk for the Mane,
And this one walks the sands again.

rumours: Rimmen sits closest to Cyrodiil and the Thalmor watch it closest. The Renrijra Krin watch the Thalmor. Everybody in Rimmen watches everybody. It is a very attentive city.
Hunters out of Rimmen went to the Hircine stones west of the city to ask for a good senche-hunt. They came back with a senche cub that follows them everywhere. The cub is now larger than the hunters.
An Imperial pilgrim from Bravil lives at the Meridia stones north of Rimmen. She burns things. Mostly the dead. This one is glad they are mostly the dead.
legends: Rimmen was built by a Khajiit queen who loved an Imperial merchant and wanted a city that faced both ways, north to his country and south to hers. She built two great gates and never decided which was the front. The citizens still argue about it.

rumours: The Mane sits in Riverhold and the Thalmor sit nearby with their hands folded. Nobody in Anequina has seen a Thalmor smile. This one thinks perhaps they cannot.
There are slavers at the Molag Bal stones south of Riverhold, taking Khajiit for the mines of the High Elves, they say. The Mane's guard says they are only rumours. The rumours have chains.
The Sanguine stones west of Riverhold had a moon-sugar revel so loud last month that the Mane's own cooks went to join it. Dinner was very late.
legends: Anequina was once a kingdom of horse-lords and desert warriors, and Pellitine a kingdom of silk and temples. The Mane married the two together, and like any old married couple they still keep separate rooms and quarrel about the cooking.

rumours: The Moon-Bishop Hadoba says the Lattice is strong this year. She says it every year. This one has never once seen her look worried, which worries this one.
A caravan came into Torval sick and coughing, from the Peryite stones north of the city. Ri'jasha the caravaneer escaped it. Her people did not. She waits in the market for a hero.
The Clavicus stones north of Torval grant wishes to merchants. Khajiit merchants are very careful how they wish. Khajiit merchants are careful how they do everything.
legends: Torval was built on the place where the moons touched the sand. The Moon-Priests say if you stand in the great court at midnight on the Two-Moons Dance, your shadow falls in two directions at once, and one of them is the shadow of who you will become.

rumours: Senchal is the city of thieves and the thieves are proud of it. Rajhin was born here, they say, the greatest thief of all. Every pickpocket in the city claims to be his great-great-grandcub.
Somebody robbed the Nocturnal stones west of Senchal. Robbed the shrine of a thief-god. Every honest thief in Senchal is furious.
Smugglers in Senchal sell anything: sugar, silk, swords, secrets. The Thalmor customs post takes a share. The Renrijra Krin take the customs post. Business goes on.
legends: Rajhin the Footpad stole a tattoo from the neck of the Empress while she slept, and sold it back to her the next morning without her ever knowing it had been missing. Senchal's thieves say this is the finest theft ever done, because nothing was harmed and everyone profited, and Rajhin got breakfast.

rumours: A warrior called Hazadir holds the Boethiah stones in the Pellitine hills and fights any who challenge him. Nine have challenged. Nine have died. All nine had their tea with him first.
The Pellitine sword-schools train their students to fight blindfolded, by smell and sound. A blindfolded Khajiit is still a better duellist than a sighted Nord, they say. Never say this to a Nord.
The jungle road south of the sword-schools floods every spring, and the caravans that wait it out always pay the same toll: one story each, told by the fire, and it had better be new.
legends: Boethra, whom the Khajiit call the Clever Warrior, taught the first Pellitine swordmasters that the strongest blow is the one your enemy does not see coming. That is why the Pellitine schools teach courtesy first: a warrior who bows deeply has already measured your stance.

imperial_city.hook: The White-Gold Tower still stands over the city that the Elves besieged in the Great War. Justiciars walk the Talos Plaza, the Arena roars, and every district hides a quarrel older than the Concordat.
imperial_city.rumour: The city's quiet these days. Quiet the way a room goes quiet when a Justiciar walks in. Keep your amulets under your shirt, friend, and your prayers under your breath.

notes.title: Justiciar's Register, Talos Plaza
notes.author: Second Emissary Calindil
pages:
#Register of Observances, Talos Plaza District
Morndas, 9th of Last Seed, 4E 201
Addressed to the Office of the First Emissary, Embassy of the Aldmeri Dominion.

Item. The household of the cloth-merchant Varus Albecius continues to keep a lamp lit on Tirdas evenings. The lamp is unremarkable. The schedule is not. Recommend a visit after the next lamp.
Item. A wall in the alley behind the Gilded Carafe bears a carved hand with nine lines. Scraped. Recarved by morning. Assign a watcher.

Item. The Imperial Watch captain of this district responds to our requests with exemplary courtesy and no results. His courtesy is to be commended. His results are to be noted.
The Concordat is not a treaty, Emissary. It is a lesson. We are merely teaching it slowly.

notes.title: Letter from the Waterfront
notes.author: Petrus Calvo
pages:
Dear Aulus,
Wages on the Waterfront are down again. The Company says the war is over and so the war rate is over. I say the war is not over if you count the Justiciars, but nobody pays me to count.

I put two drakes on the Arena last Fredas. A Nord girl called Svala the Unbending, fighting for the Yellow. She lost in a breath. The fellow beside me laughed and won thirty. He was wearing Blue. So was the referee's cousin.

Mother asks if you will come up from Leyawiin for her name-day. Bring Blackwood honey and do not bring that Argonian you play dice with, the watch here still remembers the last time.
Your brother, Petrus

bruma.hook: A Nord town on the roof of Cyrodiil, all steep slate and woodsmoke, where the Pale Pass trade runs north and the Daedric stones in the nearby hills are busier than the chapel.
bruma.rumour: Bruma folk are Nords at heart and Imperials on paper. The paper's getting thin, if you take my meaning. Mind what you say about Ulfric in the Countess's hearing.

notes.title: Notice on the Great Chapel Door
notes.author: Brother Aurel, Chapel of the Nine
pages:
^By Order of the Countess
This house is the Chapel of the Eight Divines. Petitions to the Ninth are not to be spoken, written or left in the offering box. Petitions so left will be burned unread by the priest, for the protection of the petitioner.

To the faithful, from Brother Aurel: I burn them unread. I do. But some of you write very large, and the fire is slow, and Talos forgive me, I have learned the names of half your dead this winter.
And to whoever keeps leaving wolf-pelts on the altar: the Countess knows. Stop.

notes.title: Freight Ledger of Hrodvar Ice-Hand
notes.author: Hrodvar Ice-Hand
pages:
#Second Seed
40 iron bars, for Falkreath. Paid in fur.
12 crates 'salt fish', for Helgen. Not fish.
3 crossbows, broken down, for 'the cousin'. Paid in Stormcloak silver. Melt it before spending.

#Mid Year
Toll at the Pass went up again. Legion sergeant wants a cask of mead a week to look the other way. Cheaper than silver and he can't spend it in the Imperial City.
Note: Kjeld says the road past the Molag Bal stones is bad. Three carters gone this season. Send the wagons the long way, and never at night.

chorrol.hook: A Colovian market town built around a great oak, home to the Fighters Guild hall and to more quarrels over cattle, debts and inheritance than any court in the Empire can untangle.
chorrol.rumour: Chorrol's honest, mostly. But there's a fellow here who wished his debts away at the Clavicus Vile stones south of town, and now every man he owed is in the ground. Talk to Ostorius, if you've the stomach.

notes.title: Fighters Guild Notice Board
notes.author: Clerk of the Chorrol Hall
pages:
^CONTRACTS OPEN
Goblins in the hills west of the North Country road. Twenty drakes the ear, proof required, no ears from the same goblin.
Escort wanted for a wool cart to Skingrad. Driver is deaf; shout.

Investigation wanted, discreetly: the beggars of Chorrol walk south to the Namira stones every new moon. Two have not come back. The Countess wants to know why, and she does not want to know loudly.
Refused contracts: anything involving the Clavicus Vile shrine. The Guildmaster says she's done paying funerals for clever men.

notes.title: List in a Shaking Hand
notes.author: Ostorius Varro
pages:
#Those I owed, as of First Seed
Gallus the wool-factor, 300. Dead, fell from his roof.
Widow Marcia Plautia, 85. Dead, choked at table.
Tertia of the Grey Mare, 40. Dead, kicked by her own mule.
Caius the cobbler, 12 drakes and a pair of boots. Dead. I didn't even mind about the boots.

Still living: my sister Livilla, 6 drakes, lent to me at Mother's grave so I could buy the flowers.
I said the words at the stones. 'Let what I owe be settled.' I meant paid. I meant paid. Livilla, if you read this, go to Skingrad. Go now. Don't lend anyone anything.

cheydinhal.hook: A Nibenese town of tall timber houses and a canal, half full of Dunmer who came over the Valus Mountains after the Red Year and never went home, because there was no home to go to.
cheydinhal.rumour: Cheydinhal's Dunmer now, more or less. Good neighbours, mostly, if you don't mind ash-yam stew in every kitchen. Just don't buy the empty house by the east wall, whatever price they ask.

notes.title: Roll of the Refugee Hall
notes.author: Ilvesa Dren, Hall Warden
pages:
#Arrivals, Rain's Hand
The Sarano family, six, from Kragenmoor. Two burned, one blind. Bunks four to nine.
A silt-strider herder, no name given, from Balmora. Brought the strider's harness and nothing else. Says the beast died crossing the Valus and he carried the harness for luck.

#Arrivals, Second Seed
One Ordinator, out of armour, refusing to give his name. Prays at the canal at dawn and dusk. The children are afraid of him. I am not. I have seen what he is afraid of.
Note to the Count's steward: we need blankets more than prayers. Send blankets. I will supply the prayers myself.

notes.title: Letter Never Sent to Mournhold
notes.author: Taren Sarano
pages:
Aunt Vedila,
We are in Cheydinhal. The Imperials are cold but they leave us be, which is more than the ash did. Father works the canal locks. Mother does not speak since Kragenmoor.

There is a shrine to Nocturnal west of the town where some of our people go at night. Father says the Temple would not approve. Mother went last week. She came back and slept for the first time in a year. I don't know who to thank.
If the roads open, tell me if the house still stands. Tell me even if it doesn't.

skingrad.hook: A walled Colovian city of vineyards and tomato farms on the Gold Road, ruled by a Count nobody has ever seen by daylight, and ringed by shrines to the Princes of revelry, plague and the hunt.
skingrad.rumour: Best wine in the Empire and the Count's never seen at noon. Ask me no more about the Count. Ask Galen Vinicius about his daughter instead; he's been asking everyone else.

notes.title: An Order of Wine
notes.author: Steward of Castle Skingrad
pages:
To the cellars of Galen Vinicius:
His Excellency requires forty bottles of the Weald Shiraz of the year 4E 188, to be delivered after sunset to the castle's lower gate. Not the gate on the hill. The lower gate. After sunset.

His Excellency notes with sympathy the absence of your daughter Lucilla, and observes that young persons who go dancing in the hills sometimes return, and sometimes are better not sought. He offers no further counsel.
Payment enclosed. Please do not ask the courier to stay for supper. He will refuse.

notes.title: Healer's Memorandum on the Weald Cough
notes.author: Apothecary Sabina Turro
pages: Cases this month: nineteen. All from the farms south-east of the city, all within a morning's walk of the Peryite shrine. Symptoms: dry cough, black spots on the tongue, an unnatural tidiness. Two patients folded their blankets eleven times each before I could stop them.

I have prescribed garlic and rest. I suspect the stones would prescribe something else. I am requesting a priest of Stendarr, a barrel of vinegar and, if the Count can spare one, a guard who is not afraid of farmers who cough in rows.

kvatch.hook: The city that burned first in the Oblivion Crisis is rising again, stone by stone. Its masons dig through two centuries of rubble, and not everything under the ash wants to be found.
kvatch.rumour: Kvatch is half scaffold and half ghost story. The masons turn up old things every day. Coins, bones, once a Count's own door-knocker. Sometimes the families come looking for what's theirs.

notes.title: Masons' Roster, Western Wall
notes.author: Savlian Matius
pages:
#Week of the 3rd, Sun's Dawn
Orc crew of Durga gra-Bol: 14 hands. Laid 60 courses. Asked for meat twice a week. Granted.
Imperial crew: 9 hands. Laid 22 courses. Asked for a priest to bless the foundations. Granted, grudgingly; the priest charges by the stone.

Found in the rubble by the old chapel: a strongbox, empty; a child's wooden horse; a sword with the blade fused to its scabbard by the Gate-fire. I have kept the horse on my desk. I do not know why.
Reminder: no one digs at the scar where the Gate stood. The ground there is still warm. Two centuries, and it is still warm.

notes.title: Letter of the Atrius Family
notes.author: Lucia Atrius, of Anvil
pages:
To whoever reads this, at the rebuilding:
My family were Atrius of Kvatch, glassblowers, with a shop in the lane beneath the cathedral. My great-great-grandmother fled the night the Gate opened. She buried the family seal-stone in the cellar first, because she meant to come back.

She never did. None of us did. But the story came down to me: a grey stone, palm-sized, carved with a swallow, under the third flag from the hearth. If the masons have reached our lane, I beg you, look. Bring it to the steward's table at the wall and I will pay what I can.
We are glassblowers. We are owed one thing that did not melt.

anvil.hook: A Gold Coast port of white walls and red roofs, where East Empire Company ships unload, pirates drink in the same taverns as the sailors they rob, and the old lighthouse watches the Abecean Sea.
anvil.rumour: Anvil's lovely if you like fish and gossip. The Company's hiring sailors and nobody's signing. The last crew that sailed for Stros M'Kai came back three hands short and wouldn't say why.

notes.title: Manifest of the Swift Gull
notes.author: Purser of the East Empire Company
pages:
#Inbound from Senchal, 2nd of Hearthfire
80 casks of rum, sealed. 60 bolts of Elsweyr cotton. 4 crates 'medicinal herbs', Senchal port-stamp, not opened per instruction from the Factor.
1 Khajiit passenger, name given as 'no one in particular', paid in gold, disembarked before inspection.

Note for the Factor: the medicinal herbs smell exactly like moon sugar. I have not opened them. I would like that recorded twice. I have also not seen the Khajiit since. I would like that recorded too, in case it matters later.

notes.title: Lighthouse Keeper's Daybook
notes.author: Ottavia Sene
pages:
#Turdas
Oil low. Ordered more. The Company says it will send oil when it sends wages, which is to say at the second coming of Tiber Septim.
A widow climbed the stair at dusk. The lamp guttered, as they say it does. I stood with her until it steadied.

#Fredas
She came again. She says her husband was mate on the Jolly Pocket, taken by the new pirate captain, the one who spares Kvatch flags. She says the captain is Kvatch-born and hates Anvil for taking her mother's house. If true, half the town owes that woman something and the other half owes her more.

bravil.hook: A river town of leaning shacks and skooma dens around the statue of the Lucky Old Lady, where the Niben's fog hides smugglers, dream-sellers and the shrines of madness and ruin just beyond the walls.
bravil.rumour: Bravil's no worse than any river town, it's just more honest about it. If you hear a fellow by the bridge selling sleep, keep walking. If you hear one selling buttons, walk faster.

notes.title: Prayer Pinned to the Lucky Old Lady
notes.author: Marcella, a boatwoman
pages:
~Old Lady, Lucky Lady, turn your face my way,
~Keep my hull above the water, keep the watch at bay,
~Keep my boy from Senchal sugar, keep my man from dice,
~And if you can't keep both of them, at least keep one of them twice.

Old Lady, it's me again. You turned east last night and the river men are betting that means a flood. I've put my last two drakes on 'no flood'. If you could see your way to staying dry, I'd light you a candle every Loredas till I die, and I've never once lied to you, except about the candles.

notes.title: Watch Report, West Road
notes.author: Sergeant Brennus Halo, Bravil Watch
pages: Patrol to the Dagon shrine at dusk, as ordered. Nine persons in red hoods, keeping a fire. One woman giving a sermon about 'the world unmade and made honest'. They called her Cassia. They did not appear to fear us. We appeared to fear them, which I regret.

On the way back we passed the Mad God's stones and found a soup tureen full of buttons on the altar. Constable Vibia took a button. Constable Vibia now speaks only in rhyme. I am requesting hazard pay, a priest, and a new constable.

leyawiin.hook: The southern gate of the Empire, a stone city on the Blackwood marshes where Imperials and Argonians eye each other across a river and a war neither side has properly finished.
leyawiin.rumour: Leyawiin keeps its gates shut at dusk now. Not for bandits. For the marsh folk. And for the noblewoman on the hill who's buried three husbands in black lace.

notes.title: Decree of the Count of Leyawiin
notes.author: By the Count's own hand
pages:
^Let it be known
That no Argonian of the Blackwood shall pass the river gate after the bells of dusk without a letter of surety from a citizen of Leyawiin, the said citizen to stand liable for the conduct of the said Argonian in every particular.

Under this, in chalk: 'And who stands surety for the Count?'
Under that, in another hand: 'The Count's wife, poor woman.'
Under that, scratched with a claw: 'We remember when the river was ours. We are patient. Sleep well, Count.'

notes.title: Unsigned Letter in Lilac Ink
notes.author: Lady Severa Cassinia
pages:
Darling Ottavio,
You asked why I wear black at weddings. It saves time, dearest. Nobody ever asks the bride of three seasons why she buys her mourning ahead.

I went to the spider stones west of the city on the new moon. I left a silk scarf and a secret, as one does. I came home with a name. Yours, Ottavio, was not the name. Yours was the one before it. Do be a darling and stay away from my sweets until the Lady of Whispers changes her mind.

shrine_azura_cyrodiil.hook: A tall statue of Azura in the Great Forest south-west of the Imperial City, her hands raised to the twin hours of dusk and dawn. Dunmer refugees walk out here from the capital to pray for a home they can't return to.
shrine_azura_cyrodiil.rumour: The Dunmer from the city's poor districts walk out to the Azura statue in the forest every evening. They don't beg there. They just stand, and when the sun goes they go home quieter than they came.

notes.title: A Refugee's Dusk Prayer
notes.author: Neria Dalvilo, of the Imperial City's Elven Gardens
pages: Mother of the Rose, it is Neria again. I came out of Ald'ruhn on my father's back when the mountain spoke. I am thirty now. I sweep floors in the Elven Gardens for an Altmer who calls me 'the grey girl'. He does not know my name. You do.

I do not ask you for home. Home is ash. I ask you for one dusk where I am not tired, and one dawn where I do not wake already ashamed of being glad to be alive. You took us out of the old Temple's hands once and made us your people again. Take us out of this one. Or only stay with me until the light goes.

shrine_boethiah_cyrodiil.hook: A Daedric statue of Boethiah on a windswept shelf of the Jeralls south-west of Bruma, where sell-swords from both sides of the Skyrim border settle blood-debts in a ring of trampled snow.
shrine_boethiah_cyrodiil.rumour: There's a fighting ring at the Boethiah stones above Bruma. Nords, Imperials, Redguards, all bleeding for the Prince. The Countess calls it murder. The fighters call it 'clearing accounts'.

notes.title: The Rules of the Ring of Snow
notes.author: Gunnhild the Unfriended, Keeper of the Ring
pages:
^The Ring of Snow
One. Any blood-debt may be brought here. Kin-killing, oath-breaking, stolen pay. The Prince does not care whose side you fought on. The Prince cares who walks away.
Two. No healers in the ring. No healers after, either, unless you can walk to Bruma on your own feet.

Three. Betrayal is permitted. Betrayal is admired. If your second turns on you, that is a lesson, and Boethiah loves a lesson.
Four. The winner takes the loser's boots. In the Jeralls that is not a joke.
Five. Keep the Legion out of it. Last summer's sergeant still owes the Prince a rematch.

shrine_clavicus_vile_cyrodiil.hook: A smiling statue of Clavicus Vile in the Colovian hills south of Chorrol, where desperate folk come to make wishes and leave with exactly what they asked for.
shrine_clavicus_vile_cyrodiil.rumour: Never say 'settled' out at the Clavicus stones. That's what Ostorius Varro said, and now all Chorrol knows what the Prince does with a careless word.

notes.title: Terms Scratched on a Slate
notes.author: unknown hand
pages:
^Terms of Exchange, Shrine of the Prince of Bargains
The Petitioner asks. The Prince grants. The Prince is not responsible for the Petitioner's grammar, the Petitioner's intent, the Petitioner's family, or the Petitioner's continued breath.

Under the terms, scratched deeper: 'I asked for a horse that would never leave me. It won't. It stands at the foot of my bed every night, and it is not alive, and I cannot sell the farm. Do not ask for anything with the word never in it.' Under that, in charcoal: 'Or always.' Under that: 'Or settled.'

shrine_hermaeus_mora_cyrodiil.hook: A writhing Daedric monument to Hermaeus Mora in the hills north of Cheydinhal, littered with mildewed books that scholars of the Arcane University swear they never brought here.
shrine_hermaeus_mora_cyrodiil.rumour: There's a scholar from the University living at the Hermaeus Mora stones north of Cheydinhal. He sends the town letters asking for ink. Lots of ink. More ink than one man could ever use.

notes.title: A Letter Requesting Ink
notes.author: Magister Quintus Avidius, Arcane University (on leave)
pages:
To the stationer of Cheydinhal:
Kindly forward a further twelve pots of oak-gall ink and the same of lampblack. My previous order has been consumed. I do not mean used. I mean consumed. The books here are hungry, and I have a theory, which I set out in a footnote that is, I regret to say, now four hundred pages long.

Footnote, the only one I will trouble you with: the Arch-Mage forbids the study of the Prince of Knowledge on pain of expulsion. The Arch-Mage has never stood here at midnight and heard every book open at once. If he had, he would understand why one does not leave. Do not send a guard. Send ink.

shrine_hircine_cyrodiil.hook: A great antlered statue of Hircine in the woods of the West Weald, where Skingrad's hunters leave the first heart of every season, and where something leaves heads in return.
shrine_hircine_cyrodiil.rumour: The Skingrad hunting lodge leaves a stag's heart at the Hircine stones every spring. Last spring they forgot. That's the spring old Marius got his throat opened in his own bed.

notes.title: Tally of the Weald Hunting Lodge
notes.author: Huntsmaster Corvo Aelian
pages:
#Offerings to the Huntsman, by season
First Seed: heart of a red stag. Accepted, the heart gone by dawn.
Mid Year: heart of a boar. Accepted.
Hearthfire: heart of a bear, the big sow from the ridge above Skingrad. Accepted, and the ridge silent for a month.

Evening Star: heart of nothing. The lodge voted to stop. Too old for superstition, they said.
Sun's Dawn: Marius Aelian, my brother, dead in his bed with the door barred. Paw-prints on the sill, too big for any wolf of the Weald.
I have made the offering since, alone. The lodge does not know. The Huntsman does.

shrine_malacath_cyrodiil.hook: A brooding statue of Malacath in the hills east of Kvatch, where the Orc masons rebuilding the city carve their grievances into the stone, one name at a time.
shrine_malacath_cyrodiil.rumour: The Orcs building Kvatch's walls walk out to the Malacath stones on rest-days. My brother says they carve the names of foremen who cheat them. My brother says a lot of things, but he hasn't cheated an Orc since.

notes.title: The Grudge Stone of the Kvatch Masons
notes.author: Durga gra-Bol and her crew
pages:
^Remembered before the Furious One
Foreman Tullus of the Cathedral works: kept back four days' pay at Frostfall. Paid, after the scaffold fell beside him. Name struck through.
The merchant Albus of Anvil: sold us rotten timber for the Count's gate. Not yet paid.

The priest who blessed the Imperial crew's stones and not ours: not yet paid.
The Gate itself, that burned the city we are building: paid. Two hundred years ago. By a man who walked into fire. Malacath remembers him too.
We build Kvatch with our hands. We will be remembered in it, or the walls will learn our names some other way.

shrine_mehrunes_dagon_cyrodiil.hook: A jagged statue of Mehrunes Dagon in the swampy hills west of Bravil, where red-hooded remnants of the old Mythic Dawn have gathered to preach the world's ending once again.
shrine_mehrunes_dagon_cyrodiil.rumour: Red hoods at the Dagon stones west of Bravil. The Imperial Cult's sending someone, they say. I hope it's someone big. I hope it's someone who doesn't mind fire.

notes.title: Leaf of a Red-Bound Sermon
notes.author: Ruinous Cassia
pages:
#The Third Teaching of the Unmaking
You were told the Gates failed. They did not fail. They were interrupted. A Septim broke himself to close them, and there are no more Septims. Think on that, brothers. Think on what holds the door now. A Mede. A treaty. A tower with no fire in it.

The world is a house built on a lie, and every lie is kindling. We do not need to open a Gate. We need only wait at the door with a lamp. The Prince of Change is patient as a coal. Be patient with him.
Bring oil to the next gathering. Bring a name you would like to see burn. The Prince keeps a list.

notes.title: Warning Carved on a Reed Post
notes.author: a Bravil eel-fisher
pages:
Fishers of the west bank! Do not set nets past this post. The red hoods took my brother's boat and his net and they gave him a pamphlet. He read it. He does not fish now. He sits by the fire at the Dagon stones and smiles at it.
If you go to fetch him, take a priest and two friends. Do not take a pamphlet.

shrine_mephala_cyrodiil.hook: A many-armed statue of Mephala in the Blackwood west of Leyawiin, where the city's nobility send veiled servants on moonless nights to bargain for secrets and poisons.
shrine_mephala_cyrodiil.rumour: The Leyawiin quality don't go to the Mephala stones themselves. They send a servant in a veil. My cousin went once, for her lady. She came back knowing who her lady meant to poison and has never sweetened her tea since.

notes.title: Instructions for a Veiled Errand
notes.author: S.C.
pages:
Girl,
You will walk to the spider stones by the west path, not the road. You will wear the grey veil. At the altar you will leave the silk scarf and whisper the secret I have written on the inside of your wrist. Then you will wash your wrist in the marsh.

If a voice answers you, you will memorise every word and repeat them to me and to no one else. If no voice answers, you will wait until it does.
If anyone in Leyawiin asks where you were, you were at the Chapel of Zenithar praying for a better position. You will be getting one, if you are discreet. You will be getting another kind if you are not.

shrine_meridia_cyrodiil.hook: A shining statue of Meridia on a hilltop north-east of the Imperial City, built over the bones of an Ayleid sanctuary. Its light has gone dim, and the dead are walking up the hill in a line.
shrine_meridia_cyrodiil.rumour: The Meridia statue past the Heartland farms used to glow at night like a lantern. It's dark now. A shepherd saw skeletons walking up to it in a row, and a man in black walking behind them.

notes.title: Journal of a Pilgrim of the Dawn
notes.author: Sister Aurelia Vanne
pages:
#17th of Sun's Height
I have kept the light here nine years. The Lady asks only three things: that the dead stay dead, that the light be kept, that the keeper not lie to herself. Tonight I lie to myself. I tell myself the shapes on the road are deer.

#19th of Sun's Height
They are not deer. A necromancer calling himself Corvus the Pale has camped in the Ayleid cellars beneath the shrine. He raises the old Elven dead and walks them up the hill to stand around the statue, facing it, so their unlight smothers hers. The lens in her hands has gone grey.

#20th of Sun's Height
I cannot fight him. I can only write this, and leave it where the Lady can see it. Whoever reads: break his line of dead, end him, and lift the lens from the statue's hands so its light can be kindled again. She rewards those who keep her light. She always has.

shrine_molag_bal_cyrodiil.hook: A hunched statue of Molag Bal high in the Jeralls north-west of Bruma, where chains are set into the rock and the snow around them is never quite white.
shrine_molag_bal_cyrodiil.rumour: Three carters gone on the north road this season, all near the Molag Bal stones. And now Jorunn's girl Hilde. Bruma's watch says wolves. Wolves don't use chains.

notes.title: Ledger of the Chain-Keeper
notes.author: Lady Ottilia Venn
pages:
#Accounts of the Shackled Gift
One carter, Imperial, strong back. Offered to the Lord of Domination at the Frostfall new moon. Kept forty days. Excellent.
One carter, Nord, loud. Kept nine days. The Lord prefers the quiet ones, I find, but the loud ones are more satisfying to quiet.

One girl, Bruma, called Hilde, the daughter of a tavern cook. Taken on the north road with a basket of bread. Not yet offered. She sings to herself in the cold. I have decided to let her finish the song first.
Note: the Countess's guard came within a mile last week and turned back. Send her another case of Skingrad red. Keep her drinking.

shrine_namira_cyrodiil.hook: A crouching statue of Namira in the hills south-east of Chorrol, where the town's beggars hold a feast every new moon and nobody in Chorrol asks what is served.
shrine_namira_cyrodiil.rumour: Every new moon the beggars of Chorrol walk out to the Namira stones and come home well fed. Two didn't come home last month. The other beggars say they were 'invited to stay'.

notes.title: Hymn of the Gutter Sisters
notes.author: Old Fennia, Queen of the Chorrol Gutter
pages:
~The fine folk step around us, the fine folk hold their nose,
~The fine folk give a copper and they wipe it on their clothes,
~But the Lady of the Leavings sets a table in the stone,
~And she never once has asked us what we're doing on our own.

To the two who stayed, Septimus Crow and Big Arelia: you were good company and better eating company, and I hope the Lady keeps you warm down in the dark. Nobody in Chorrol will miss you. That's why she loves you. That's why she loves us all.
Next feast: the new moon of Rain's Hand. Bring your own spoon.

shrine_nocturnal_cyrodiil.hook: A hooded statue of Nocturnal in the woods west of Cheydinhal, where Nibenese thieves leave a coin before every big job and Dunmer refugees come to pray for a little shadow to hide in.
shrine_nocturnal_cyrodiil.rumour: No thief in the Nibenay works a big job without leaving a coin at the Nocturnal stones west of Cheydinhal first. The Gray Fox did, they say. My uncle did, and he's never been caught. He's never been paid either.

notes.title: Chalk Marks Beneath the Statue
notes.author: many hands
pages:
^Shadow hide you.
Beneath it, a ladder of chalk marks, each with a coin-mark beside it: 'Dorian, the Bravil counting-house, done.' 'Little Mouse, the Chorrol wool-factor, done.' 'Teeth, the Skingrad castle cellar, NOT done, Teeth is not with us now.'

Newest of all, in a careful hand: 'Taren's mother. She came to pray for sleep. Leave her be, all of you, or answer to me. She is not ours, but the Lady listened to her anyway. A shadow is a shadow, whoever stands in it.' The coin beside it is Morrowind silver.

shrine_peryite_cyrodiil.hook: A dragon-shaped statue of Peryite in the farmland south-east of Skingrad, where a strange cough has begun to spread through the vineyards, and its victims have begun to keep their houses unnaturally tidy.
shrine_peryite_cyrodiil.rumour: The sick from the farms near the Peryite stones sweep their floors three times a day and line their spoons up by size. My aunt caught the cough and alphabetised her chickens.

notes.title: The Orderly Diary of Tullius Sarn
notes.author: Tullius Sarn, tomato-farmer
pages:
#1st of Hearthfire
Cough began. Swept the yard. Swept it again. The stones by the road are untidy. I have rearranged them. They are better now.

#4th of Hearthfire
Wife says I talk in my sleep about 'the Taskmaster's ledger'. She does not understand that every sickness is a list and every list must be completed. I have walked to the shrine and set the offering bowls in a straight line. The dragon approves. The cough approves.
#5th of Hearthfire
Nineteen sick. Twenty is a rounder number. I will visit my sister.

shrine_sanguine_cyrodiil.hook: A leering statue of Sanguine in the vineyard hills between Skingrad and Kvatch, where an endless revel is said to wait for any guest who takes the first cup.
shrine_sanguine_cyrodiil.rumour: There's always music near the Sanguine stones in the Weald, even when nobody's there. Galen Vinicius's daughter followed it on her name-day. That was a month ago.

notes.title: A Perfumed Invitation
notes.author: The Host
pages:
To Lucilla Vinicius, who is far too clever for her father's cellar:
You are invited to a gathering in your honour in the hills west of Skingrad. Wear the green. Bring nothing. Leave nothing behind but your name-day and your good sense.

There will be wine you have never tasted, music you will never stop hearing, and company who will never tire of you. Arrive at moonrise. The door is the statue; knock with a full cup.
P.S. Your father's Shiraz is adequate. Ours is better. You may tell him so yourself, if you ever see him again.

shrine_sheogorath_cyrodiil.hook: A grinning statue of Sheogorath in the reeds north-west of Bravil, with a soup tureen of buttons for an offering bowl and a gentleman scamp in a borrowed hat for a doorman.
shrine_sheogorath_cyrodiil.rumour: The Mad God's stones by Bravil have a doorman now. A scamp in a feathered hat. My neighbour Fulvius swears it's his hat. Fulvius has also sworn he's a teapot, so who can say.

notes.title: A Formal Complaint
notes.author: Fulvius Pell, formerly of Bravil, presently of his own head
pages:
To the Management:
On the night of the 6th I left a button at your shrine, per local custom. In exchange you took my shadow and gave me a cat's. It is a fine shadow, it chases moths, but it is not mine and it will not sit for supper.

Further, your scamp has my hat. My good hat, the green with the heron feather. He wears it at an angle that I consider provocative. I demand the hat's return. My shadow you may keep, as I have grown fond of the cat's.
Anyone reading this who is braver than me, which is everyone: please get my hat. I will pay in buttons. Also money.

shrine_vaermina_cyrodiil.hook: A dark statue of Vaermina in the Nibenay marshes between Bravil and Leyawiin, where a dream-seller harvests sleepers lying in the reeds and sells their nightmares in Bravil's skooma dens.
shrine_vaermina_cyrodiil.rumour: Sleepers in the reeds by the Vaermina stones. Dozens. Eyes moving under the lids. The dream-woman from Bravil walks among them with a sack, and she never looks tired.

notes.title: The Dream-Seller's Book
notes.author: Mother Lethe
pages:
#Harvest, the 3rd of Frostfall
Sleeper by the long reed: a fisherman. Dreamt of drowning. Common stock. Two drakes the hour.
Sleeper by the stone: a Legion veteran. Dreamt of the Red Ring. Rare stock. Twenty drakes the hour, and the Bravil gentlemen fight over it.

Sleeper under the willow: a child. Dreamt of her mother. I did not take it. I am not a monster. I took the one after, when she dreamt of the Prince instead.
Note: the Lady of Nightmares grows impatient with the small stock. She asks for a dreamer of rank. A priest, perhaps. Or one of those fine Leyawiin ladies who never sleep at all.

mournhold.hook: The capital of Morrowind, a city of domes and gardens in the Deshaan where the Grand Council meets, the Temple keeps its old splendour, and the scars of the Argonian border wars are hidden under fresh paint.
mournhold.rumour: Mournhold's grand again, if you don't look too close. The Argonians burned the lower city in the last border war. We rebuilt it in stone. Priestess Ilvari still looks south every evening, toward what they took.

notes.title: Proclamation of the Grand Council
notes.author: Clerk of the Grand Council of Morrowind
pages:
^By the Grand Council, in session at Mournhold
It is resolved that the southern border with the so-called Kingdom of Argonia shall be patrolled by levies of the Great Houses in rotation. House Redoran in Morning Star and Sun's Dawn. House Indoril in First Seed and Rain's Hand. House Hlaalu...

...House Hlaalu, having declined to name a month, is assigned all the remaining months by default, until such time as it learns to attend council.
It is further resolved that the Twilight Stone of Deshaan, taken from the shrine of the Lady Azura in the border raids of 4E 158, remains a matter of honour for every House, and that a reward stands for its return. The reward has stood for forty-three years.

notes.title: Letter Found in a Garden Lantern
notes.author: Davena, a gardener's apprentice
pages:
Uvren,
The new stone in the lower city is pale. It looks like a scar on the old black. The masters say it will darken with ash in thirty years. I don't want to wait thirty years. I want it to look like home now.

Priestess Ilvari came through the gardens this evening and stood by the south wall till the sun was gone. I asked her what she was looking at. She said 'something of the Lady's, in the hands of something that isn't'. Then she gave me a twilight rose to plant. It took. It's the only thing this season that has.

notes.title: The Bazaar and the Temple: A Short Guide
notes.author: Lisara Tervyn, palace archivist
pages:
#Names worth knowing
Archcanon Teris Ulvani receives visitors in the temple courtyard and asks for nothing. Mistress Hlaren runs the Great Bazaar's guild stall and stamps contracts. Old Sedyn leads a lantern into Old Mournhold every Sundas and has never been lost. Gaela Nelvan serves cold tea at the Silver Samovar whenever someone is listening.

#What the guide does not say
The Silver Samovar's back table is where deals are made. Orlen Veloth's smithy opens when he has stopped shouting at the anvil. Ravos Dren is a student of public architecture; keep your purse in your hand. The palace archive has a second basement. We have all agreed that it does not.

vivec.hook: The great canton city on the water south of Vvardenfell, seat of the Archcanon and the Morag Tong, where pilgrims climb the stairs of the Temple and every canton is a town with its own feud.
vivec.rumour: Vivec's cantons still stand, those the sea didn't take. Walk the bridges at night and you'll hear three languages, four prayers and at least one Morag Tong writ being read out loud.

notes.title: A Pilgrim's First Day in Vivec
notes.author: Brother Llevel of the Foreign Quarter
pages: Welcome, pilgrim. You will want to go everywhere at once. Do not. The cantons are larger than they look and the bridges are longer than they feel, and the guar-hide sandals sold in the Foreign Quarter will not last the climb to the High Fane.

Do pray at the shrines of the Tribunal. Do not pray aloud at the shrines of the old Daedra, the Reclamations, even though the Temple honours them now. The older priests still flinch.
Do not ask an Ordinator for directions. Do not ask a Morag Tong agent anything at all. If someone in the Arena canton offers you a good price on anything, it is not a good price.

notes.title: Rent Ledger of the Hlaalu Canton
notes.author: Crassius Curio's under-steward
pages:
#Rents collected, Hearthfire
The Dren cousins, ground floor: paid in full, with a note complaining of the smell of the Waterworks. Complaint filed under 'water'.
The Argonian fishmonger Sweet-Tail: paid in full in fish. Fish accepted at market rate minus the smell.

Unit 14, upper tier: unpaid three months. The tenant is a 'scholar of the Boethiah stones' and says he will pay when the Prince of Plots grants him a fortune. Councillor Curio says to leave him be, as he finds the man amusing. I find him behind in his rent. We are both right.

notes.title: A Visitor's Directory of the Hlaalu Canton
notes.author: Tosa the Cantonkeeper
pages:
#Who is where
Warden Telyne Aryon keeps the canton stairs, mornings, and knows which are loose. Tosa the Cantonkeeper minds the water-gates; find her at low tide, never at flood. Brother Fendil sells blessings on the Temple stairs at any hour that has pilgrims. Hlenil Dro ferries to every canton and will not discuss what lies under the water.

#Inns, shops and small secrets
The Sunken Lantern (Ruvene Olvyn) charges by the flight of stairs to your room; she has counted them all. Bethal's Dry Goods and Wet Alibis sells umbrellas in a city where it never rains. The handles are hollow. Do not ask. The Last Stair at the Palace gate is a wall; the hospice behind the shrine, sixteen cots, is not.

balmora.hook: The Hlaalu town on the Odai river, where silt striders groan at the port, the Camonna Tong owns half the doors, and sleepers have begun to walk out of the ash at night toward the Vaermina stones.
balmora.rumour: Balmora's all business, bad business mostly. Ask Fevyn Andalor about her brother. She'll tell you about the ash-sleepers, and about the Vaermina stones north-east, and she'll cry, and she'll ask you for help.

notes.title: Warning Nailed to a Door
notes.author: unsigned
pages:
OUTLANDER,
This house was sold to you by a Hlaalu clerk who did not ask us. We are asking now. You have until the next Tirdas to sell it back to its rightful buyer for the price you paid, less the cost of our trouble.

If you are wondering who we are, ask the Imperial who had the house before you. You will find him in the Odai, a little downstream. Bring a pole.
This is a courtesy. The Tong is courteous once.

notes.title: Fevyn's Night-Book
notes.author: Fevyn Andalor
pages:
#Night of the 2nd
Drals got up at the second hour and walked to the door with his eyes open. I said his name. He said 'the Mother is singing'. Our mother is twelve years in the ground.

#Night of the 5th
Tied him to the bed. Woke to find the rope bitten through and the door open. Found him at the edge of town at dawn, facing north-east, toward the Vaermina stones, standing in a ring of others. All sleeping. All smiling.
#Night of the 6th
I am going to ask the outlanders at the Council Club. One of them might be mad enough to walk up there.

notes.title: Factor, Fence and Ferry: Balmora by Name
notes.author: Port-Master Orrel
pages:
#The people of the river
Factor Dron Hlaalu keeps the Council Manor and the river with equal care. Nilena Vandas is a freight consultant on the south bank and will tell you she has never held anything for anyone. Hesta Girith the apothecary sells poultices and, on quieter days, apologies. Rilvo Aleth of the Legion watches the high bridge and will tell you to keep to the left.

#Eating, drinking and being cheated
Eight Plates serves eight plates a night; the ninth guest goes hungry. It is a policy, not a shortage. South Wall Cornerclub has rules about singing before sundown and cheating after; everything between is a negotiation. The silt strider called Dowager has been known to sit on caches of silk. Do not tell her she is brave.

aldruhn.hook: The Redoran city of the Ashlands, built in and around the shell of a giant emperor crab, where ash storms rattle the shutters and Daedric shrines stand within sight of the councillors' windows.
aldruhn.rumour: Ald'ruhn's Redoran to the bone: duty, honour, and a dry cough. If you're headed north of town, mind the Nocturnal stones; the Bal Molagmer meet there, and they don't like strangers seeing their faces.

notes.title: Ash Storm Watch Report
notes.author: Hlaren Morvayn, Redoran Guard
pages:
#Night watch, Skyrim gate
Storm began at the first hour. Visibility nil. Three knocks at the gate at the second hour. Did not open, per standing order. No footprints in the morning. The ash covers footprints. That is the official explanation.

Second item. A Telvanni mouth arrived at dusk, asked the road to the Hermaeus Mora stones west of the city, and was given it, as the road is public. He has not returned. Councillor Sarethi asks whether we are obliged to look for him. Councillor Venim asks whether we are obliged to stop looking if we find him.

notes.title: Letter to a Son in the Legion
notes.author: Ranis Athrys
pages:
Garyn,
You write that Cyrodiil is green and wet and that nobody coughs. I am happy for you. Here the ash is so thick this year we eat it in our bread and call it pepper.

Your sister has joined the Redoran Guard. She says she is protecting the house. She is protecting a wall. But she is good at it, and the wall is still standing, and so is she.
Come home when your service ends. Bring Imperial tea. Do not bring an Imperial wife, your father is too old for the argument.

notes.title: A Roster of the Shell
notes.author: Rolfa Skar-Guard
pages:
#The Council and the town
Councilor Brara Redoran sits in the Skar and counts honour like debt. Captain Rolfa Skar-Guard keeps the gate and explains rules slowly. Brarmin the egg-miner knows the tunnels under the town and does not whistle. Tevra Dren the apothecary sells marshmerrow and, she says, no poisons. Durgul Ash-Born duels for hire and insists he is no assassin.

#Inns and secrets
The Rat in the Pot has a pot and no rat. There was a rat; it is on the sign, and has recently been given a very small crown. The Ald Skar Inn's smith, Velan Arethi, will replace any chitin plate he did not break. The shell hums three notes on certain nights. The third is wrong.

sadrith_mora.hook: The Telvanni town on an island off the east coast, where giant mushroom towers house the most powerful and least neighbourly wizards in Morrowind, and every contract has a clause you didn't read.
sadrith_mora.rumour: Sadrith Mora's safe enough if you keep your eyes down and your hands where a wizard can see them. Never, ever sign anything they hand you in the Gateway Inn.

notes.title: Contract of Service to a Telvanni Mouth
notes.author: Clerk of Tel Naga
pages:
^Articles of Hire
Article 1. The Hireling shall perform such errands as the Master sees fit.
Article 7. Errands may include the gathering of reagents, the carrying of correspondence, the testing of potions and the being of a subject.
Article 12. 'Subject' shall be understood in the broadest sense.

Article 19. The Hireling waives all claim to the shape the Hireling began service in.
Article 31. The Master is not liable for spores.
Article 40. The Hireling acknowledges having read all forty Articles. The Hireling, by signing, also acknowledges Articles 41 through 60, which are written in an ink visible only by the light of Secunda.

notes.title: Complaint to Mistress Dratha's Steward
notes.author: Garoth Velas, fisherman
pages:
Honoured Steward,
The Mistress's tower has been coughing spores onto the harbour for nine days. My nets are white with them. My catch has grown little caps. My wife's hair has grown a little cap. I ask, with every respect, that the Mistress be asked to cover her tower's mouth.

I understand that the Mistress does not answer petitions from fishermen. I understand that the Mistress has a long memory. I would point out, respectfully, that I also have a long memory, and a boat, and I know which rocks the Mistress's supply ships like to avoid.

notes.title: Towers, Spores and Rooms That Move
notes.author: Dalyne Hlaren of the Gateway Inn
pages:
#Who lives where
Magister Gaenor Dreth levitates above the Council Spire and is perpetually bored. Magister Ulveni Rathra keeps fourteen floors, eleven guardians and a singing teapot at Tel Naga. Skeema the Sporekeeper tends the greenhouses and will tell you not to look at the grey ones. Apprentice Veya carries slippers up fourteen floors and would like to learn something else.

#Rooms and rumours
Every window of the Gateway Inn shows somewhere; room nine has recently shown a woman in a green shawl. Fennik Sul's Spore & Sundry sells fumigation salts and asks that glowing jars be closed again. Sergeant Maro Gallus keeps the Wolverine Hall garrison and the Legion's distance from the towers.

ebonheart.hook: An old Imperial fortress-port on the Stonefalls coast, black-walled and salt-stained, where the East Empire Company and the Legion hang on in Morrowind with fewer men every year.
ebonheart.rumour: Ebonheart's all Legion and Company, which these days means half a garrison and a lot of unpaid ledgers. Go to the docks if you want work. Go to the Sanguine stones south-east if you want a party.

notes.title: Garrison Strength, Ebonheart
notes.author: Tribune Marcus Salvo, Legion of Morrowind
pages:
To the Legate at Cyrodiil:
Strength this quarter: one hundred and twelve, of whom nineteen are sick, eleven are Dunmer levies who answer to their Houses before me, and four are, frankly, too old to hold a spear upright.

The Argonians patrol their bank of the border openly now. They wave. I have ordered my men not to wave back. My men wave back.
I repeat my request for two cohorts. I would accept one. I would accept a single competent sergeant. I would accept a letter telling me that anyone in the Imperial City remembers Ebonheart is still ours.

notes.title: Ebonheart Dock Ledger
notes.author: Canctunian Ponius's clerk
pages:
#Arrivals, Last Seed
The Abecean Rose from Anvil: wine, salt, and an inspector from the Company's head office. Inspector given the best room and the worst figures we could find, so as to set expectations.

#Departures, Last Seed
The Ondusi Gull for Windhelm: kwama eggs, saltrice, three crates of 'Telvanni pottery'. The pottery hums. Passengers: two Orc masons for the Malacath festival, one widow, one Bosmer who would not stop asking whether the ship was haunted. It is not. That we know of.

notes.title: Bastion and Quarter: Who Is Who
notes.author: Chaplain Loris
pages:
#Garrison and Company
Legate Corvus Pello wants order and a name by evening. Chaplain Loris hears the garrison's confessions, which are short. Felmin Rothal at the Company Hall will discuss margins openly; it is the only thing the Company does not hide. Guardsman Tolan Veyl keeps the south gate and an eye on his mother's medicine.

#The Quarter and its fixers
Aryn the Informer stands lower than anyone else and charges for the view. Marga Ironhand's Bastion's Heel serves two kinds of beer; ask for the one the garrison pretends it does not drink. Three guards salute a stone in the ash-flowers each dusk. Nobody has mentioned it to the Legate.

necrom.hook: The holy city of the dead on Morrowind's eastern coast, where every Dunmer family hopes to rest, pilgrims walk the bone-lined streets, and grave-robbers have begun to steal ancestors for Daedric rites.
necrom.rumour: Somebody's breaking urns in the City of the Dead and carrying the ashes off. The priests are frantic. Mortician Mirvala says the robbers camp near the Mad God's shrine, where pilgrims don't walk.

notes.title: An Appeal from the Mortuary
notes.author: Mortician Mirvala Sadri
pages:
To any pilgrim, sellsword or Ordinator who reads this:
