In the last month, eleven urns have been broken in the lower catacombs and the ashes carried off. Among them, the urn of Ancestor Llaren Indavel, who founded this mortuary and who has not been moved in seven hundred years.

We know where they go. The robbers sell to Daedra-worshippers, and they camp in the hollow by the Sheogorath shrine north-west of the city, because pilgrims will not walk that road. Recover Llaren's urn. Bring it to me at the mortuary. The rest of the dead will forgive us. Llaren will not, and he is not quiet when he is displeased.

notes.title: Diary of a Pilgrim from Narsis
notes.author: Selyn Ules
pages:
#Arrived Necrom
The city is bone-white and silent. The priests walk softly. A child asked me whose grandmother I had come to visit. I said mine. She said 'which one?' and pointed down. I did not sleep well.

#Second day
Laid Mother's ashes in the Ules alcove. The alcove was already full. The priest said 'they'll make room', and something below the floor shifted. I gave a larger donation than I had planned. I suspect that is how the mortuary is funded.

notes.title: A Pilgrim's Reckoning of the Row
notes.author: Mirele Sathil of the Pilgrims' Rest
pages:
#The living of the Row
Keeper Salvu hears the dead and passes on the polite ones. Elder Nerevi guards the Row and lets no outlander in without a guest list. Aldrin the Restless has dug four hundred graves and will not dig one more. Tadrik Ulvo sells shrouds, urns and sympathy cards, with no refunds.

#Candles, counts and one small secret
The Pilgrims' Rest sets out forty-one candles each night and finds forty-two each morning. The extra belongs to a girl who never reached the shrine. Say her name aloud. It helps. Mind the third step of the Row; the elder's husband did.

red_mountain.hook: The volcano at the heart of Vvardenfell, still smoking two centuries after the Heart was broken and decades after the Red Year. Ash storms, ash creatures, and the Ghostfence are all that stand between it and the island.
red_mountain.rumour: Don't climb the mountain without an Ashlander guide and a Temple blessing, and even then, don't. Sleepers walk down from it in the storms. Whatever's up there isn't finished with us.

notes.title: Journal of an Ash Pilgrim
notes.author: Dovyn Aren, of Suran
pages:
#First day of the climb
My Ashlander guide left me at the foot of the slope. She said, 'from here the mountain is your guide'. She did not say whether it was a good one.

#Second day
Ash to my knees. A shape followed me all afternoon at the edge of the haze, too tall to be a man, too still to be a beast. When the wind cleared, there was nothing. There were footprints, though. Bare. Pointing up the mountain, not down.

#Third day
I reached the bowl of water the pilgrims leave below the crater. It was full. Someone had filled it today. Someone up here drinks. I am going on. If I do not come down, tell the Temple that the mountain is not empty. Tell them it is listening.

notes.title: Standing Orders for the Mountain Watch
notes.author: Tharen Veloth, Temple Ordinator
pages: All patrols on the mountain slope will move in fours. No patrol will follow a voice in the ash. If a voice calls you by your name, you will answer only with the Litany of the Three, aloud, until it stops.

Sleepers found on the slopes are to be restrained and carried to the Ghostfence, not slain, unless they are no longer what they were. The distinction is yours to make. The Temple trusts you to make it. The Temple will also judge you if you make it wrongly. Walk with Vivec.

shrine_azura_morrowind.hook: A great statue of Azura in the Deshaan east of Mournhold, beloved by Dunmer since before the Tribunal. An empty socket in its base marks where the Twilight Stone sat until the Argonians carried it off.
shrine_azura_morrowind.rumour: The Lady's statue east of Mournhold lost its stone to Argonian raiders. The socket's still there, black and empty. Priestess Ilvari in Mournhold has heard where it went. She needs someone brave enough to cross the border.

notes.title: Prayer Carved Around the Empty Socket
notes.author: the keepers of the shrine
pages:
~Mother of Dusk, we have kept your light without its heart,
~Lamp without flame, cup without wine.
~Forty winters we have turned to the south at sunset,
~And forty springs the south has not answered.

Below, more recent, in a firm hand: 'The Stone is in Black Marsh, in the hands of rot-eaters who worship the Lady of Decay, at her stones in the Shadowfen south of here. They use it to light their feasts. I am too old to go. I will find someone who is not. Ilvari, priestess, Mournhold.'

shrine_boethiah_morrowind.hook: A statue of Boethiah on the Ascadian Isles between Balmora and Vivec, the Prince who freed the Chimer, where Hlaalu councillors come by night to pray before they ruin one another.
shrine_boethiah_morrowind.rumour: The Hlaalu say they pray at the Boethiah stones for wisdom. What they mean is for a good knife. Watch whose palanquin goes out on the night before a council vote.

notes.title: A Councillor's Private Petition
notes.author: unsigned, sealed with a Hlaalu ring
pages: Prince of Plots, who taught Veloth's people to leave the old gods and follow the new, I ask nothing so grand. I ask for Councillor Dravos's majority on the canal tariff.

I have bought three votes. He has bought four. I know which of his four are for sale twice. You taught us that loyalty is a garment, not a skin. Give me the patience to wait for him to take it off.
I leave you a dagger that has never been used, because you like potential. I will come back with it when it has been.

shrine_clavicus_vile_morrowind.hook: A statue of Clavicus Vile in the West Gash hills between Balmora and Ald'ruhn, where miners of the Caldera ebony diggings come to wish for one more good vein.
shrine_clavicus_vile_morrowind.rumour: A Nord miner from Caldera wished at the Clavicus stones for a vein that would never run dry. It hasn't. He hasn't come up in four months. They send down bread on a rope.

notes.title: Letter Sent Up on the Bread Rope
notes.author: Bjorn Hollow-Eye, ebony miner
pages:
To the foreman, and to whoever goes to the stones next:
The vein doesn't stop. That's the trouble. Every time I think I'll stop, there's another seam just there, black and fat, and my hands go to it before I can think. The Prince said 'never run dry'. He didn't say the vein. He meant me.

Send bread, and send a priest who isn't afraid of Daedra, and if neither will come, send the next fool who wants to wish for something. I'll tell him what I learned. Never wish for a thing to go on. Wish for it to end well. The Prince can't do much with 'well'. He hates the word.

shrine_hermaeus_mora_morrowind.hook: A tentacled monument to Hermaeus Mora in the Ashlands west of Ald'ruhn, where Telvanni wizards come to trade secrets they'll regret and Ashlanders leave their dreams so the Prince won't come for them.
shrine_hermaeus_mora_morrowind.rumour: A Telvanni mouth walked out to the Mora stones west of Ald'ruhn and hasn't walked back. The Ashlanders say the Prince of Secrets keeps what he's given. The Redoran say good.

notes.title: Notebook of a Telvanni Mouth
notes.author: Arvil Sethan, Mouth of Tel Naga
pages:
#Bargain the first
Offered: the name of my master's apprentice who poisons him slowly. Received: the third word of the binding my master uses on his doors. A fair trade. The apprentice would have been caught regardless.

#Bargain the second
Offered: my mother's face. I did not think I would miss it. Received: the location of a Dwemer vault under the Ashlands. I cannot picture her now. I picture the vault.
#Bargain the third
Offered: the way home. Received: everything. I am going to sit here a little longer and read. The ink is moving. It is beautiful. Tell Tel Naga I have resigned.

shrine_hircine_morrowind.hook: A beast-headed statue of Hircine on Azura's Coast west of Sadrith Mora, where Telvanni hunters and Ashlander trackers meet at the Huntsman's altar and argue over who has the right to the season's great prey.
shrine_hircine_morrowind.rumour: There's a kagouti on the coast as big as a silt strider calf, with a tusk broken like a crown. The hunters call it Ashtusk. Hircine's chosen, they say. Nobody who's hunted it has come back with the tusk.

notes.title: The Huntsman's Challenge, Posted at the Altar
notes.author: Ulath Morvel, Telvanni huntsman
pages: To all who hunt on Azura's Coast: the Huntsman has marked his prey for this season. A bull kagouti, called Ashtusk by the Zainab trackers, with one tusk snapped into a crown. He grazes in the scrub north of this altar and he has killed four hunters and a guar-herd since Rain's Hand.

The rules of the Huntsman's season are old and simple. Hunt him with your own hand. Take the crowned tusk, not the head. Lay nothing at this altar but the hunt itself. The Ashlanders say whoever brings down Ashtusk will run with the Huntsman's favour until the next Bloodmoon. I say whoever does it will also be paid, by me, if I am still alive to pay.

shrine_malacath_morrowind.hook: A statue of Malacath in the Deshaan hills east of Ebonheart, one of the four corners of the Dunmer House of Troubles, where Orcish dockhands and exiled Dunmer outcasts swear oaths of vengeance side by side.
shrine_malacath_morrowind.rumour: The Temple calls Malacath a Corner of the House of Troubles and sends Ordinators to watch his stones. The Orcs from the Ebonheart docks go anyway. So do a lot of Dunmer who've been thrown out of their Houses.

notes.title: Oath of the Unhoused
notes.author: Erur Dralor, once of House Dres
pages: I was Dres. My House cast me out for refusing to sell an Argonian child I had raised as my own. My House says Malacath is a curse, a Corner of the House of Troubles. My House should know. It made me his.

Prince of the Spurned, I swear: I will not beg my House to take me back. I will build a new one, of the cast-out and the cursed, and it will outlast theirs. I swear it on the iron of my father's ring, which I melted, and on the name of the child, whom they sold anyway.
Below, in Orcish: 'We heard you, grey brother. Come drink with us at the docks.'

shrine_mehrunes_dagon_morrowind.hook: A spiked statue of Mehrunes Dagon in the lava fields of Molag Amur west of Necrom, where a cult that blames the Red Year on the Tribunal's weakness preaches ruin and recruits from the refugee camps.
shrine_mehrunes_dagon_morrowind.rumour: Five Ordinators went to clear the Dagon stones west of Necrom. Four came back. The cult there calls itself the Unbroken Ash and says the Red Year was Dagon's mercy. Its leader's a Dunmer named Sul Indaram.

notes.title: Report of the Necrom Ordinators
notes.author: Ordinator Sereth Arvel
pages:
To the Archcanon, by way of the Necrom chapter:
We approached the shrine at dusk, five strong. Twelve cultists, two summoned dremora, and their speaker, Sul Indaram, a refugee from Kragenmoor who lost his family in the ash. He preaches that the Tribunal failed us and that only the Prince of Destruction is honest about the world.

Ordinator Dral fell to the dremora. His mask was taken, and the cult wears it at their rites to mock the Temple. We withdrew. We are not enough to try again.
I request that the Temple seek outside help. Kill Indaram. Recover Dral's mask. A mask of the Ordinators must not be worn by heretics in sight of Necrom's dead.

notes.title: Sermon of the Unbroken Ash
notes.author: Sul Indaram
pages: The Three told you they held up the sky. Then the moon came down. The Three told you they held back the mountain. Then the ash came down. The Three told you they would always be with you. Where are they?
Mehrunes Dagon never lied to you. He promised fire, and he gave it. He promised ruin, and here it is. There is a terrible comfort in a god who keeps his word. Come and warm your hands at it.

shrine_mephala_morrowind.hook: A many-armed statue of Mephala on the southern shoulder of Red Mountain, sacred to the Morag Tong, whose agents climb here to renew their vows in the Webspinner's shadow.
shrine_mephala_morrowind.rumour: The Morag Tong climb to the Mephala stones under Red Mountain every season to renew their vows. Lately there are spiders nesting there, and the Grandmaster is not pleased.

notes.title: Vow of a Morag Tong Initiate
notes.author: an initiate of the Morag Tong
pages: Webspinner, Mother of the Threads, I come to your shadow under the mountain with a sanctioned writ in my hand and no hatred in my heart. I kill by the law of the Houses and the writ of the Tong. I kill so that the Houses need not go to war.

Let my hand be quiet and my thread be short. Let my target know my face, as the law demands, and let them not see it twice.
Added in another hand: 'The threads of the shrine are gone. Spiders where the threads were. Brothers and sisters, be wary at the altar. Eno Hlaalu is seeking them.'

shrine_meridia_morrowind.hook: A radiant statue of Meridia in the Deshaan east of Mournhold, where a zealot who calls the Dunmer's ancestor guardians abominations has begun smashing family shrines in the Lady's name.
shrine_meridia_morrowind.rumour: There's a Meridian zealot in the hills east of Mournhold who's broken six ancestor shrines this year. Says the guardian spirits are undead and the Lady wants them freed. The families want him dead.

notes.title: Tract of the Cleansing Light
notes.author: Brother Vanel Orethi, Servant of the Radiance
pages: Grey folk, hear me. You bind your dead to your doorsteps and call it love. You trap your grandmothers in bone and ash to guard your silver and call it reverence. The Lady of Infinite Energies calls it what it is: a prison of the dead, kept by the living.

I do not break your shrines in hate. I break them so that your ancestors may go into the Light at last, as they were always meant to. You will curse me. They will thank me.
Scrawled across the bottom: 'My grandmother asked to stay, you fool. She chose. Come near the Llethan tomb again and you will meet the Light sooner than you planned.'

shrine_molag_bal_morrowind.hook: A hulking statue of Molag Bal in the Ascadian Isles between Balmora and Vivec, a Corner of the House of Troubles, where vampires of the old Vvardenfell clans are said to come to pay homage to their father.
shrine_molag_bal_morrowind.rumour: Somebody left a heart at the Molag Bal stones south of Balmora. A Dunmer heart. The Ordinators say a vampire clan's moved in from the Ashlands. The plantation folk lock their shutters by dusk now.

notes.title: Field Notes of a Vampire Hunter
notes.author: Galsa Indrano, of the Ordinators (retired)
pages: Signs at the shrine: fresh blood on the left hand of the statue, none on the right. That is the Aundae custom, offering with the hand that does not hold the knife. The Quarra would leave nothing; the Berne would leave a body.

So: an Aundae coven, refined, patient, thinks itself above the brute clans. They will have a manor, or a plantation house, with a host who never eats at his own table. Check every Ascadian estate where the field hands have grown pale and the master has grown young. I am too old to do it. Someone is not.

shrine_namira_morrowind.hook: A statue of Namira in the West Gash scrub between Balmora and Ald'ruhn, where the blighted, the scarred and the unwanted of Vvardenfell gather in a ragged congregation that the Temple cannot bring itself to disperse.
shrine_namira_morrowind.rumour: The ash-scarred beggars of Balmora walk north to the Namira stones on feast days. The Temple won't move them on. Too many of them are Temple pilgrims who came back from the mountain changed.

notes.title: Song of the Scarred
notes.author: Nalvos the Blistered
pages:
~They turn their eyes when we go by, the ash has kissed our skin,
~They give us alms with gloves on and they will not let us in.
~But the Lady of the Unloved does not flinch to see our face,
~She keeps a seat for every scar, and every scar its place.

We were pilgrims once. We climbed the mountain for the Three and the mountain sent us back with blisters where our faces were. The Temple feeds us. The Temple will not touch us. Namira touches us. That is all the theology a beggar needs.

shrine_nocturnal_morrowind.hook: A cloaked statue of Nocturnal in the Ashlands north of Ald'ruhn, where the Bal Molagmer, Dunmer thieves who rob only those who wrong the poor, meet in the ash storms to choose their marks.
shrine_nocturnal_morrowind.rumour: The Bal Molagmer meet at the Nocturnal stones north of Ald'ruhn when a storm comes in. They choose a councillor, and by spring that councillor is a lot poorer and a lot quieter.

notes.title: Marks Chosen in the Storm
notes.author: the Bal Molagmer
pages:
^Under the Lady's cloak, in the storm of the 9th
Councillor Dravel of the Ald'ruhn Hall: took the Andas family's land for a debt that was already paid. Mark. Take the deed and burn it on his own hearth.
The Hlaalu factor at the Ald'ruhn bazaar: weights his scales with lead. Mark. Take the lead. Leave the scales.

The Redoran Guard captain who beats beggars at the gate: mark, but gently. Take his boots. He can walk in the ash as they do.
To the Lady of Shadows we give a tenth of all taken. To the Andas family we give the rest. To the councillors we give nothing at all, which is what they gave.

shrine_peryite_morrowind.hook: A dragon-shaped statue of Peryite on Azura's Coast west of Sadrith Mora, where a Telvanni healer studies the blight that crawls down from Red Mountain and has started to wonder whether it can be ordered rather than cured.
shrine_peryite_morrowind.rumour: A Telvanni healer lives at the Peryite stones west of Sadrith Mora. Says the blight is a language and she's learning to speak it. The fishermen won't sell her fish anymore.

notes.title: On the Grammar of Blight
notes.author: Mistress Ovyna Telvayn, healer
pages: Observation. Ash-blight does not spread at random. It moves in rows, like a farmer sowing. It favours the third house in a street, then the sixth, then the ninth. A Daedra of pestilence and order would understand this. Peryite understands this.

Hypothesis. If the blight is a sentence, then it can be finished. If it can be finished, it can be ended. If it can be ended, it can also be begun, by someone who knows the grammar.
Note to myself: burn page two before the Archmagister's mouth visits. He will not understand the difference between a cure and a weapon. Neither, some nights, do I.

shrine_sanguine_morrowind.hook: A statue of Sanguine in the Deshaan near Ebonheart, where sailors, Legion deserters and bored young nobles of House Indoril hold revels that start at dusk and end only when someone has sold something they shouldn't.
shrine_sanguine_morrowind.rumour: The Sanguine stones south-east of Ebonheart have a party every Fredas. My cousin went once. Came back with a new tattoo, no boots, and a deed to a ship he's never seen.

notes.title: Diary of a Company Clerk
notes.author: Aulus Petronius, East Empire Company
pages:
#Fredas
Went to the revel at the stones with Tribune Salvo's adjutant. He said it would be a lark. It was a lark. I drank something purple that an Indoril lady poured into my mouth from a shell. Then I danced. I do not dance.

#Loredas, dawn
I have woken by the statue with a hangover the size of Vvardenfell and the Company seal-ring on someone else's finger. A Khajiit's. He was snoring. I took it back. He woke and called me 'partner'.
I do not know what I have signed. I am very afraid it was a cargo of Ebonheart's entire winter salt.

shrine_sheogorath_morrowind.hook: A grinning statue of Sheogorath on the pilgrim road north-west of Necrom, a Corner of the House of Troubles, where travellers walking alone swear the stone asks after their families by name.
shrine_sheogorath_morrowind.rumour: Don't walk past the Mad God's stones on the Necrom road alone. It talks to you. It asks after your mother. And now there are grave-robbers camped in the hollow behind it.

notes.title: Pages from a Pilgrim's Wandering
notes.author: Hlenil, who walked alone
pages: It asked me how my mother was. I told it she was dead. It said, 'Oh, I know, I meant how is she being dead? Is she enjoying it?' I said I didn't know. It said I should ask her, it's only polite, and then it told me where she's buried, which was not where I buried her.

I dug at the place it said. I found a jar of pickled scuttle and a note in my mother's hand that said 'I knew you'd look'. I have not been sane since, but I have been much happier. The grave-robbers in the hollow wanted to know what the stone told me. I told them it was asking after their mothers too. They didn't like that.

shrine_vaermina_morrowind.hook: A statue of Vaermina on the western shoulder of Red Mountain, where a priestess calling herself the Dream-Mother draws the ash-sleepers of Balmora and Ald'ruhn to stand in a ring and feed her their nightmares.
shrine_vaermina_morrowind.rumour: The ash-sleepers walk to the Vaermina stones under the mountain and stand in a ring, smiling. There's a woman in the middle singing. Fevyn Andalor in Balmora says her brother is one of them.

notes.title: Lullaby of the Dream-Mother
notes.author: Dream-Mother Sadri
pages:
~Sleep, little ash-child, the mountain is near,
~Dream me your dying and dream me your fear,
~Give me the fire and give me the fall,
~And Mother will keep them, and Mother keeps all.

The mountain sends them to me, the sleepers. Something under the Ghostfence calls them, and I only stand between and catch what spills. Their dreams are red and full of the old Sixth House songs. The Lady of Nightmares drinks them like wine. I keep the best in a glass vial for myself. One taste, and you see the Heart.

stormhold.hook: An old Imperial walled town sinking slowly into the Black Marsh, where the Shadowscales keep their enclave, the King's envoy signs royal contracts, and Lukiul clerks still keep the Empire's ledgers out of habit.
stormhold.rumour: Stormhold's where the King's business is done, when it isn't done in the dark. Mind your manners at the gate and don't ask the Elder anything you don't want answered.

notes.title: Customs Ledger, Kept Out of Habit
notes.author: Tullus-Ei, Lukiul clerk
pages:
#Customs, Stormhold Gate, Second Seed
One Khajiit caravan: spices, silk, moon sugar (declared as 'cooking sugar'). Duty assessed: none, as there is no longer any duty. Recorded anyway.
One Imperial missionary of Stendarr: three books, one bell. Asked to see the governor. Told there is no governor. Recorded his disappointment.

Note to myself: my grand-hatchling asks why I keep this book when the Empire is gone. I tell her the Empire is not gone; it is only somewhere else. She tells me that is what the Saxhleel say about the dead. Perhaps the Empire and the dead have more in common than I would like. I will keep the book a little longer.

notes.title: Notice of the Royal Envoy
notes.author: Teeba-Enoo, Royal Envoy of the King of Argonia
pages:
^By the King's word
All Saxhleel held in debt-service on the lands of any foreigner are free from this day, and the debts are void. Any foreigner who disputes this is invited to dispute it with the Envoy in Stormhold, in person, at dusk.

The Envoy notes that few have accepted this invitation. The Envoy notes that those who did were persuaded. The Envoy wishes all foreigners a pleasant and lawful stay in the King's marsh, and reminds them that the marsh has a very long memory and very many eyes.

notes.title: Two Hills, One Bridge: A Directory
notes.author: Bridge-Wife Soft-Step
pages:
#People of the stones
Warden Scales-Her-Chains keeps the bridge and the peace between the hills. Stone-Carver Nook carves what is not the stone and refuses to touch the idol. Scout Fast-Eyes sees much and says a tenth. Pebble-Pocket sells rope, hook, oil and boots, and will not sell the gorge.

#Beds and a quiet secret
The Two Hills Rest has a door for each ziggurat and soup on the bridge. Do not drop the bowl. The sleeping idol of the north hill has one eye very slightly open, and the south hill carved it so. The old White Rose prison holds one elder who wishes only to be asked a question.

gideon.hook: A former Imperial plantation town on the edge of the Black Marsh, its grand houses gutted by vines and Saxhleel salvagers, its Mages Guild chapter clinging on with a handful of stubborn scholars.
gideon.rumour: Gideon's quiet these days, except for the stone-cutters. The Mages Guild there lost a scholar at the Mora stones near Stormhold, and the Guildmaster's offering a reward for her journal.

notes.title: Last Ledger of the Vellarius Plantation
notes.author: Overseer Galenus Vellarius
pages:
#Saltrice harvest, 4E 172
Hands in debt-service: 61. Hands escaped: 4. Hands returned: 0. Hands that the King's envoy calls 'free subjects of Argonia': 61. I have written to the Governor. There is no Governor.

#Last entry
The hands did not riot. They did not burn the house. They simply put down their tools at noon, all together, and walked into the marsh. The envoy came at dusk and read me a paper. I am leaving for Leyawiin tonight. Let the vines have the ballroom. They were always better dancers than my wife.

notes.title: Notice from the Gideon Mages Guild
notes.author: Guildmaster Cyrus Aemilius
pages: Reward offered for the recovery of the field journal of Adrienne Lirrian, Associate of the Guild, who travelled to the Daedric monument of Hermaeus Mora west of Stormhold to study the alleged intertwining of a Hist root with the monument's stone.

Associate Lirrian is presumed lost. Her assistant, Kassus, returned to Gideon, briefly, and then left again in the night for the shrine, reciting what we believe to be page numbers. If he is found, do not argue with him. He knows things now that do not bear arguing with. Bring the journal. Bring Kassus too, if he still answers to his name.

notes.title: The Plateau by Name
notes.author: Magistrate Lucia Verrus
pages:
#Water, grain, law
Well-Keeper Dusk measures the Basin Well each dusk and each dawn and trusts nobody's plumb-line. Granary-Mother Seshi knows each person's debts by their pockets. Watcher Tamtam has watched for rain for eleven years. Magistrate Lucia Verrus keeps the courthouse and will not discuss the goat.

#Inn and clay
The Stable Steed feeds the guar first; it is economics, not discrimination. Nesa Clay-Hand makes pots and one very ugly, much-loved idol. Twyllbek ruins hold a lead tube with the grant to the Eastern Cut. It belongs to the road.

helstrom.hook: A Saxhleel border town on the edge of the Shadowfen, closest of all Argonian towns to Morrowind, where the old chains of the slave years lie at the bottom of a black pool and the warriors never quite put down their spears.
helstrom.rumour: Helstrom's touchy about Dunmer. Fair enough, really. If you've got grey skin, smile a lot and don't talk about Necrom. And stay off the paths to the shrines north of town.

notes.title: Knot-Message of the Helstrom Watch
notes.author: Walks-Ahead, Warden of the Northern Paths
pages:
Written down by the Lukiul scribe from the knots, as spoken:
Seven nights past, the paths by the noisy stones north of town. Footprints of Dunmer boots, heavy, as if carrying. Two of our hunters, Neeta-Lei and Old Breathes-Slow, did not come home from the egg-pools.

At the Molag Bal stones, a fire. Voices in Dunmeri. A chain, new iron, on the ground. Walks-Ahead says: this is not raiding. Raiders take and run. This is someone who means to stay. The Warden asks the Shadowscales for help. The Shadowscales say they are busy. The Warden asks anyone with a spear.

notes.title: Words Carved by the Black Pool
notes.author: the warriors of Helstrom
pages:
^Here we sank the chains
In the year the mountain burned we went north. We went to the houses where our grandparents were kept. We did not take gold. We took the chains, every one we could find, and we brought them home, and we gave them to the water.

The water turned black and has stayed black. The elders say it is the chains rusting. The young say it is the water refusing to forget. Both are true. Any Saxhleel may come here and drop a stone for an ancestor who wore iron. The pool is very full of stones.

notes.title: Rebuilders and the Ring: A Roll
notes.author: Mason Noo
pages:
#Who lifts what
Rebuilder Pa-Dar wants to know why the ninth stair stops at the sky. Mason Noo measures twice and still apologises to the stone. Elder Teeba remembers where the stairs led and has told no one. Kessa Rope-Walker sells rope, pitch and plumb, and will not discuss the bridge.

#Beds and a stair
The Broken Ring's roof is new and its walls are old. The rope-walks sway; the long one has won a week's pay for a nameless stranger. The ninth stair needs a black wedge from a jar marked with a spiral. It is in the mason's old yard.

lilmoth.hook: The capital of Argonia, a port city of reed-roofed towers and drowned Imperial stone, where the King holds court without a crown and the harbour mud hides the Empire's last customs strongbox.
lilmoth.rumour: Every diver in Lilmoth's tried for the old customs strongbox in the harbour mud. Thirty years of Imperial bribes, they say. The slaughterfish like that patch of water. A lot.

notes.title: Letter of the Last Customs-Master
notes.author: Quintus Mallo, Imperial Customs-Master of Lilmoth
pages:
My dear Vibia,
The Empire is leaving Lilmoth and I am leaving with it, though my strongbox is not. The Argonians stand on every pier and watch us pack. I cannot carry it past them without awkward questions, and every answer would get me hanged in two provinces.

So I have sunk it. Off the end of the old customs pier, in the shadow of the harbour tower, where the water is deep and the fish are large. Thirty years of 'gifts', my love. If I do not come back for it, tell our son. Tell him to bring a long hook and a short temper, because the slaughterfish there are the size of dogs and twice as loyal.

notes.title: Report from a Thalmor Observer
notes.author: Aldarion, Third Secretary, Aldmeri Mission (unofficial)
pages:
To the Mission in Alinor:
I have attended the so-called court of the so-called King of Argonia. There is no throne. There is a tree. The King sits beneath it and listens to petitioners who speak to the tree, not to him. When I asked to be presented, I was told that the tree had already been informed of my presence and was considering it.
I recommend we not attempt anything in Lilmoth. Every Argonian in the room looked at me at once when I entered, and I am quite certain none of them turned their heads.

notes.title: Canals, Boats and Who Rows Them
notes.author: Boatwife Mudtoe
pages:
#Names on the water
Keeper Sees-Many-Moons tends the Hist pool. Boatwife Mudtoe knows every canal's name and mood. Trader Ocheeva imports Cyrodiilic cloth and wine and regrets it. Tribune Lucius Varro counts what comes in and refuses to accept that it does not match. Sap-Fence Ruu sells the not-sacred kind of sap, by the thimble.

#Beds, bowls and small debts
The Dripping Reed asks guests to say where they are going; the canals are patient, not forgiving. A rice merchant on the fourth canal keeps seven debt-boats and a second ledger in the rafters. The fourth canal's old tenant is bad-tempered but not yet hungry. Keep to the left of every bend.

murkmire.hook: A cluster of Saxhleel villages deep in the southern marsh, where the paths shift with the water, egg-thieves raid the hatcheries, and every village keeps its memory in a single chosen child.
murkmire.rumour: Murkmire's the true marsh. Tah-Weesh the Egg-Keeper's been robbed again, and the Archeins and the Bright-Throats are feuding over a canoe. Go with a guide or don't go at all.

notes.title: Egg-Keeper's Tally Knots, Written Down
notes.author: Tah-Weesh the Egg-Keeper
pages:
^Spring clutch, the village of the Bent Hist
Eggs laid: forty-one. Eggs hatched: thirty-three. Eggs that sleep and will not hatch: three. Eggs taken by thieves in the night: five.
Tah-Weesh says: the thieves took the five best. They knew which ones. Someone told them.

The Bright-Throat clan says it was the Archeins. The Archeins say it was the Bright-Throats. Tah-Weesh says it was a foreigner who paid someone in this village with Imperial silver. Tah-Weesh says: when I find who, the Hist will remember them, but I will not.

notes.title: Letter of a Lost Cartographer
notes.author: Hieronymus Brisk, Imperial Geographical Society
pages:
Dear Society,
I have mapped the path from Lilmoth to Murkmire four times. It has been a different path each time. My guide says the path did not change; I did. I have asked him to clarify. He says I will understand when I hatch.

I enclose all four maps. Please file them together under 'Murkmire, approaches, provisional'. Please do not send another cartographer. Please do send boots. Mine have been adopted by a family of frogs, and the village elders say it would be rude to reclaim them.

notes.title: What Is Said and Not Said in Murkmire
notes.author: Child Pip
pages:
#The people
Elder Nulaa keeps the fire in the middle of the spiral. Hunter Teek hunts in silence and has found that most things can wait. Rice-Mother Mussa grows three crops a year and says you are too thin. Pip is a child, and talks more than the rest together.

#The path
Every child walks the spiral once and brings a coal back to their own door. You do not speak. You do not drop the coal. Nobody tells what the fire said. The north paddy had a frog in a noble's collar; the scarecrow wears it now.

shrine_azura_black_marsh.hook: A moss-draped statue of Azura in the marsh west of Stormhold, kept by Saxhleel who were once slaves in Morrowind and learned the Lady's name from the very masters they escaped.
shrine_azura_black_marsh.rumour: The old freed-slaves go to the Azura stones west of Stormhold at dusk. They learned her from the Dunmer. Funny thing, to keep your master's god. They say she was never the master's.

notes.title: Prayer of One Who Was Kept
notes.author: Seven-Scars, once of a Dres plantation
pages: Lady of Dusk, the Dunmer who kept me prayed to you every evening and beat me every morning. I listened to the prayers. I thought: if she is their god, she is a cruel one. Then one evening my master prayed for a good harvest, and that night the river took his fields.

I do not think you were ever theirs. I think you were waiting for them to deserve you, and they did not. So here I am, a free Saxhleel, at your stones in the marsh, and I bring you the only thing I own that I chose for myself: this evening. Take it. It is a good one. The light is very gold.

shrine_boethiah_black_marsh.hook: A spear-scarred statue of Boethiah in the marsh west of Stormhold, where Saxhleel veterans of the northern war tally what they took back from Morrowind and what it cost them.
shrine_boethiah_black_marsh.rumour: The veterans of the northern war go to the Boethiah stones and cut marks into the statue. One mark for each chain broken. One for each friend lost. The statue's very scarred.

notes.title: Tally Cut into the Statue's Base
notes.author: Huzei, called Breaks-Iron
pages: Boethiah, Prince of the Turned Knife, the Dunmer say you taught them to overthrow their old gods. We listened. We learned. We turned the knife they taught us, and we turned it back on them, in the Red Year, when their mountain had them on their knees.

Marks for chains broken: thirty-one. Marks for friends lost: eleven. Marks for things done in the Dunmer towns that I will not tell my hatchlings about: I will not cut those. You know them, Prince. You were there. You were smiling. I was too, and that is why I come here instead of the Hist.

shrine_clavicus_vile_black_marsh.hook: A crumbling statue of Clavicus Vile in the marsh north-west of Stormhold, raised by an Imperial governor who bargained with every Prince in turn to survive the swamp and lost to all of them.
shrine_clavicus_vile_black_marsh.rumour: That Clavicus statue west of Stormhold was built by an Imperial governor who wished he'd never die in Black Marsh. He didn't. They found him in Cyrodiil, ten days after he left, drowned in a bathtub.

notes.title: Fragment of the Governor's Journal
notes.author: Governor Aulus Teretius, Imperial Province of Black Marsh
pages:
#Second year of my governorship
Azura would not answer. Boethiah laughed. Hermaeus Mora asked a price I will not write down. The little Prince of Bargains, at least, is a gentleman. He asked only what I wanted.

I said: 'I do not want to die in this swamp.' He smiled with his dog's teeth and his own, and the deal was struck.
#Fourth year
I am leaving Black Marsh tomorrow. I am going home to Cheydinhal at last. I have ordered a hot bath for the evening of my arrival. Ten years of mud, and at last, clean water. I can hardly wait.

shrine_hermaeus_mora_black_marsh.hook: A tentacled monument to Hermaeus Mora in the marsh south-west of Stormhold, through which an ancient Hist root has grown, so that the sap that weeps from the stone is full of whispering.
shrine_hermaeus_mora_black_marsh.rumour: There's a Hist root growing through the Mora stones west of Stormhold. The sap that drips off it whispers. A Breton scholar went to listen. Now her assistant's out there, reading pages that aren't there.

notes.title: Last Page of Adrienne Lirrian's Journal
notes.author: Adrienne Lirrian, Associate of the Mages Guild
pages:
#Day nineteen at the root
The Hist and the Prince of Knowledge are not at war here. They are bargaining. The root offers memories, the memories of every Saxhleel who ever drank its sap. The stone offers to keep them forever. I have been reading the bargain as it is written, in the sap, one drop at a time.

#Day twenty
Kassus has stopped eating. He sits at the root with his mouth open and catches the drops and recites. I wrote down what he said. It was my mother's name, and the day she died, and the words she said, which I never told anyone.
#Day twenty-one
I am going to taste the sap. If I do not come back, my journal is under the root. Take it to Gideon. Do not read it on the way.

shrine_hircine_black_marsh.hook: A beast-headed statue of Hircine in the Shadowfen east of Cheydinhal, where a deserter from the Legion, cursed with the Huntsman's blood, has begun hunting Saxhleel hunters for sport.
shrine_hircine_black_marsh.rumour: There's a wolf in the Shadowfen that walks on two legs and wears the scraps of a Legion tunic. He hunts our hunters. He leaves their spears stuck in the ground at the Hircine stones, like trophies.

notes.title: A Hunter's Account, Written Down
notes.author: Sings-in-Reeds, Saxhleel hunter
pages: Written by the Lukiul scribe, as spoken: The Huntsman's stones are an old place. Saxhleel hunters have left a feather there after a good hunt for longer than the Empire has been an Empire. It is a fair thing, a feather. The Huntsman likes fair things.

Now there is something at the stones that is not fair. A man who becomes a wolf, a man who was a soldier of the Empire, who ran from his legion and ran into the Huntsman's blood. He does not eat what he kills. He sets their spears in the mud by the statue, points up, and waits for the next. Five spears now. One of them was my brother's. Hunt the hunter. The Huntsman, I think, would like that.

shrine_malacath_black_marsh.hook: A statue of Malacath in the Shadowfen south of Mournhold, where the Naga, the marsh's outcast raider-clans whom other Saxhleel will not shelter, swear war-oaths to the Prince of the Spurned.
shrine_malacath_black_marsh.rumour: The Naga swear their oaths at the Malacath stones south of Mournhold. Even other Saxhleel don't go there. The Naga don't care who's spurned them. They're spurned by everybody, and proud of it.

notes.title: Naga War-Oath, Cut in Mud-Brick
notes.author: the Naga of the Long Teeth
pages:
^To the Prince Who Was Thrown Out
The Hist would not keep us. The villages would not keep us. The King would not keep us. We keep ourselves.

We swear on our teeth, which are long, and our hunger, which is longer: we will take from the Dunmer what they took from us, and we will take from the villages what they refused us, and we will take from the King nothing at all, because he has nothing we want.
We are the Naga. We are what is left when everyone else has been kind. Prince of the Spurned, we are your favourite. Say it.

shrine_mehrunes_dagon_black_marsh.hook: A jagged statue of Mehrunes Dagon in the Shadowfen just south of the Morrowind border, where Dunmer prisoners of the northern war were once held, and where their scratched messages still cover the stone.
shrine_mehrunes_dagon_black_marsh.rumour: The Dagon stones near the Necrom border were a pen for Dunmer prisoners in the war. The scratches are still on the stone. Saxhleel don't read Dunmeri, mostly. That's probably for the best.

notes.title: Scratches in Dunmeri on the Statue's Base
notes.author: Dunmer prisoners of 4E 6
pages: Day 9. Penned here at the Destroyer's stones like guar. The lizards think it fitting. Perhaps it is. My House prayed to the Three. The Three are gone. Who is left but the one who burns?

Day 31. Varel prayed to the statue tonight. Begged for fire to take the lizards. Fire came: a fever. It took Varel.
Day 40. They are letting us go. A trade, for their own taken north. I will walk home to Necrom past the stones. I will not look at the statue. I will not thank it. But I will remember it was the only god who answered, and that it answered the way it always does.

shrine_mephala_black_marsh.hook: A spider-limbed statue of Mephala in the Shadowfen south of Necrom, where Dunmer spies and Saxhleel informers leave coded messages in the webs for each other's masters to find.
shrine_mephala_black_marsh.rumour: Dunmer agents leave messages at the Mephala stones south of Necrom, folded in silk. Saxhleel agents leave other messages in the same spot. Sometimes they're the same agents.

notes.title: Silk-Folded Message, Partly Decoded
notes.author: the Weaver
pages:
To the Grey Thread, in Necrom:
The Shadowscales lost two of their own this month to ambushes on the Helstrom paths. They suspect a traitor in their enclave. They are right. You know which. I know which. Let them hunt for it a while longer; a frightened enclave is a careless one.

In exchange: the name of the Morag Tong agent who walks the Helstrom paths with a writ for the Elder. I enclose it, woven into the second fold. Burn the silk after reading. If you do not burn it, Mephala will know, and so will I, and of the two of us, I am less forgiving.

shrine_meridia_black_marsh.hook: A gleaming statue of Meridia in the Shadowfen south of Mournhold, where an Imperial missionary has spent twenty years trying to burn the bog-dead out of the marsh one wraith at a time.
shrine_meridia_black_marsh.rumour: There's a mad old Imperial at the Meridia stones in the Shadowfen. Hunts bog-wraiths with a lamp and a mace. He's not wrong, you know. There are a lot of bog-wraiths. There are fewer now.

notes.title: Letter to the Chapel of Stendarr, Cheydinhal
notes.author: Brother Felix Orvo
pages:
Brothers,
You sent me to Black Marsh twenty years ago to bring the Saxhleel to Stendarr. They declined, politely, and gave me a canoe. I have since found a better use for my faith. The marsh is full of the restless dead, drowned Kothringi, slavers who sank in their chains, travellers who took the wrong path.

The Lady Meridia, whose stones I live beside, hates the walking dead even more than Stendarr does. I hope you will forgive me for borrowing her light. It is very bright and it works. Ninety-three wraiths laid to rest. I keep a tally on the statue. The Saxhleel have started to bring me tea.

shrine_molag_bal_black_marsh.hook: A hulking statue of Molag Bal in the Shadowfen near the Necrom border, where a Dunmer slaver of an old fallen House has returned to chain Saxhleel captives in the Prince of Domination's name.
shrine_molag_bal_black_marsh.rumour: There are Saxhleel in chains at the Molag Bal stones by the Necrom border. Real chains, new iron. A Dunmer with a Hlervu ring calls himself the Chain-Lord. Helstrom wants every spear it can find.

notes.title: Orders of the Chain-Lord
notes.author: Varis Hlervu, called the Chain-Lord
pages:
To my hirelings:
We hold nine. We will hold twenty by the next Bloodmoon. Keep them chained at the statue; the Lord of Domination likes to see his gift kept close. Feed them enough to walk. Not enough to run.

My House was ruined in the Red Year and the lizards' war. We were Dres cousins, wealthy, respected, served. Now I am a beggar in Necrom, and the Saxhleel have a king. I do not accept it. Molag Bal does not accept it. He has promised that what was taken from House Hlervu will be returned in chains.
If the Helstrom warriors come, kill them. If a stranger comes, kill them faster.

shrine_namira_black_marsh.hook: A crouching statue of Namira in the Shadowfen south of Mournhold, where a cult of rot-eaters gathers to feast by the light of a pale stone that was stolen from the Dunmer long ago.
shrine_namira_black_marsh.rumour: The rot-eaters at the Namira stones feast by the light of a pale stone that glows at dusk. Stolen off the Dunmer, they say. Somebody in Mournhold would pay well to have it back.

notes.title: Feast-Song of the Rot-Eaters
notes.author: the Rot-Eaters of the Shadowfen
pages:
~What falls in the water, the water will keep,
~What dies in the marsh will go down deep,
~And the Lady of Leavings sets her table there,
~With a stone from the north for a candle-flare.

We took the pale stone from the grey folk's goddess when the raiders went north. It burns at dusk, only at dusk, a little sad light. The grey folk loved it. We love it more, because it is stolen, and stolen things are the Lady's favourite: the leftovers of someone else's love. Whoever comes for it will join the feast. One way or another.

shrine_nocturnal_black_marsh.hook: A hooded statue of Nocturnal in the Shadowfen east of Cheydinhal, where Cyrodiilic smugglers and Saxhleel born under the Shadow both leave offerings, each insisting the Lady is really theirs.
shrine_nocturnal_black_marsh.rumour: The smugglers who run the Cheydinhal-Shadowfen paths leave a coin at the Nocturnal stones. The Shadowscales leave something else there. Nobody's sure what, and nobody's asking.

notes.title: A Smuggler's Note, Left Under a Stone
notes.author: Varo 'Quiet-Boots' Arruntius
pages:
Partner,
The route through the Shadowfen to Cheydinhal is clean this month. Coin left at the Lady's statue as usual. I noticed someone else had been there before me: a black feather, a single scale, and the shape of a hand pressed in the moss where nobody's hand could reach.

I think the Shadowscales use the Lady's stones too. I think they're telling us something: that the shadow is theirs and we're guests in it. I'm going to be a very polite guest from now on. Leave two coins next time, not one. Leave three if you've been rude to an Argonian lately. I have.

shrine_peryite_black_marsh.hook: A dragon-shaped statue of Peryite in the Shadowfen south of Mournhold, raised long ago by the last of the Kothringi as the Knahaten Flu killed them, in the hope that the Taskmaster would spare an orderly people.
shrine_peryite_black_marsh.rumour: The Peryite stones in the Shadowfen are Kothringi work, the last thing they built before the Flu took them all. Saxhleel won't touch the stones. They say the Flu sleeps in them still.

notes.title: Kothringi Plea, Silver-Inlaid
notes.author: the last scribes of the Kothringi
pages: Taskmaster, Lord of the Ordered Plague, we have kept our ledgers. We have counted our dead in rows. We have buried them in straight lines. We have done everything a tidy people can do. We ask you to see that we are tidy, and to pass us by.

Added below, in a shakier hand: 'The Saxhleel do not sicken. The Imperials do not sicken. Only we sicken. If this is your order, we do not understand it.'
Below that, in a single silver line: 'There are four of us left. We will finish the inscription tomorrow.' The inscription ends there.

shrine_sanguine_black_marsh.hook: A leering statue of Sanguine in the Shadowfen south of Mournhold, where border smugglers of both races meet for revels so wild that, for one night a month, Dunmer and Saxhleel forget they hate each other.
shrine_sanguine_black_marsh.rumour: There's a revel at the Sanguine stones on the border every full moon. Dunmer and Saxhleel, dancing together. By morning they've remembered they're enemies. But the night's the night.

notes.title: An Invitation Scrawled on Bark
notes.author: the Revel-Keepers
pages: To all smugglers, deserters, poets and other undesirables of the Shadowfen and the Deshaan: the full moon revel will be held at the Prince's stones as usual. Bring drink. Bring music. Leave your grudges at the treeline; there is a pile there, you will find it.

Rules: no blades past the treeline. No talk of the Red Year. No talk of the chains. Anyone who starts a fight will be made to dance with the Naga, and they do not let go. Dunmer bring the wine, Saxhleel bring the sap. The Prince brings the rest. You'll know it when it arrives.

shrine_sheogorath_black_marsh.hook: A grinning statue of Sheogorath in the Shadowfen south of Necrom, kept by a Saxhleel who drank sap from a Hist that was struck by lightning and has been talking to the Mad God ever since.
shrine_sheogorath_black_marsh.rumour: There's an old Saxhleel at the Mad God's stones who drank sap from a lightning-struck Hist. He tells fortunes. They're all wrong. And then, a year later, they're all right.

notes.title: Prophecies of Drinks-the-Lightning
notes.author: Drinks-the-Lightning
pages: The lightning hit the Hist, and I drank the burnt sap, and the Hist said 'oops'. Then a voice that was not the Hist said 'oh, I like this one'. That was the Mad God. He likes me. I like him. We talk about fish.

Prophecies, this month: a Dunmer will bring me a pie. A King will sneeze. A Khajiit will sell the moon. A stranger will read this and think 'he is mad'. All will come true; one already has. The God says to tell you that you are standing on his foot. You are not. But you will move, now, won't you? There, he says. Good.

shrine_vaermina_black_marsh.hook: A dark statue of Vaermina in the Shadowfen east of Cheydinhal, where Saxhleel who drink Hist sap for its visions wake to find that someone else has been dreaming in their place.
shrine_vaermina_black_marsh.rumour: Hist-sap dreams are sacred to the Saxhleel. Near the Vaermina stones east of Cheydinhal, they've gone wrong. Hunters wake with nightmares that aren't theirs, in voices they don't recognise.

notes.title: Dream-Record of a Sap-Taster
notes.author: Tree-Minder Okan-Ei
pages: I drank the sap at my egg-tree and slept. In the sap-dream I should have seen my ancestors. Instead I saw a Breton woman burning in a tower I have never seen, and a voice laughed and said 'thank you, little lizard, she was delicious'.

I woke at the Vaermina stones. I did not walk here. Three others woke beside me. All of us had the same dream. The Lady of Nightmares is drinking the sap-dreams through us, like a mosquito through a reed. I will not taste the sap again until the elders find a way to close the reed.

rimmen.hook: A walled Khajiit city on the northern edge of Elsweyr, facing Cyrodiil, where Thalmor overseers, Imperial traders and the laughing rebels of the Renrijra Krin all watch each other over the same market stalls.
rimmen.rumour: Rimmen is a fine city for watching. The Thalmor watch the gates, the Renrijra Krin watch the Thalmor, and the merchants watch everybody's purses. Watch your own, friend.

notes.title: Notice of the Aldmeri Trade Office
notes.author: Overseer Ilmendil, Aldmeri Trade Office, Rimmen
pages:
^By arrangement with the Mane
All caravans entering or leaving Rimmen shall present their goods at the Trade Office for inspection. Moon sugar shall be declared by weight. Weapons shall be declared by number. Grievances shall be declared in writing, and will be filed.

Beneath, in claw-scratched Ta'agra, translated by a helpful passer-by: 'Grievances are filed. Then they are burned. This one has filed eleven. Here is the twelfth: the Overseer's purse is heavier on Fredas than on Morndas. The Renrijra Krin will be happy to file it for him.'

notes.title: Letter to a Cousin in Leyawiin
notes.author: Rawan-dar the Caravaneer
pages:
Cousin Ja'darri,
This one writes from Rimmen, where the spice road is bad and the Thalmor are worse. A caravan cannot move three hours without a new paper to stamp. This one has learned to forge the stamps. The forgeries are better than the real ones. The Thalmor have praised them.

If you are still in Leyawiin, tell the Count's wife the silk she ordered is coming. Tell her it is coming slowly because the road passes the Mephala stones and this one will not go near them at night. She will understand. That woman understands everything she should not.

riverhold.hook: The seat of the Mane, spiritual leader of all Khajiit, in the dry hills of Anequina, where the Thalmor are received with honey and silk and sent home with nothing at all.
riverhold.rumour: The Mane sits in Riverhold and smiles at the Elves. A Khajiit smile has many meanings. You should hear the Mane's guard laugh after the envoys leave.

notes.title: Dispatch of an Aldmeri Envoy
notes.author: Envoy Telarnil, to the Thalmor in Alinor
pages: Third audience with the Mane. I was received with great warmth. I was offered tea, then a second tea, then a recital of Khajiit poetry that lasted two hours and concerned a sand-flea. At the end the Mane thanked me for my patience and dismissed the court.

I have still not been permitted to raise the matter of the Rimmen tariffs. I suspect I never will be. I also suspect the poem was about me. Recommend we send someone the Mane dislikes; it may be the only way to be taken seriously.

notes.title: Mane's Guard Duty Roll
notes.author: Captain Shazar-ri of the Mane's Guard
pages:
#Duties, the week of Hearthfire
Gate: Ja'zhar, Ma'dara, the twins. Thalmor escorts: J'riss, who smiles best. Dungeon: nobody, because there is nobody in it, because the Mane does not keep prisoners, because the Mane is merciful.

Special: Ra'vinni to ride south to the Molag Bal stones and see if the slaver-rumours are true. He is to look and not fight. He is a Cathay-raht and will fight anyway. Send Do'sara with him to drag him home.
Special: someone ask the cooks why they keep going to the Sanguine stones. It is becoming a problem with the soup.

torval.hook: The capital of Elsweyr and holy city of the Moon-Priests, where the Temple of the Lattice crowns the hill, moon sugar is blessed in great vats, and the Two-Moons Dance fills the streets each year.
torval.rumour: Torval is the holiest city of the Khajiit, and the busiest. The Moon-Bishop is blessing sugar, the caravans are selling it, and poor Ri'jasha in the market is begging someone to go to the Peryite stones.

notes.title: On the Blessing of Moon Sugar
notes.author: Moon-Priest Ahnissi
pages: Moon sugar is the moonlight that falls on the sand of Elsweyr and is caught by the cane. It is holy. To eat it is to taste the Lattice. To boil it into skooma is to taste the Lattice too much, and fall through.

The sugar of the Temple fields is blessed each night under the moons by three priests, who sing the Riddle'Thar until the vats glow. Unblessed sugar is still sweet. But only blessed sugar remembers where it came from, and so the one who eats it remembers too.
This is why the skooma-cooks raid our fields. They do not want sugar. They want to forget, and blessed sugar is the hardest to make forget.

notes.title: Notice for the Two-Moons Dance
notes.author: Moon-Bishop Hadoba
pages:
^The Two-Moons Dance comes.
All are welcome in the great court of Torval at the rising of both moons. Bring a lamp for the dead. Bring a song for the living. Do not bring skooma; the Temple guard will take it, and they will not give it back, and they will look very happy.

To the pilgrims from Cyrodiil: the dance is not a performance. You will be asked to join. To refuse is not an insult, but it is noticed, and the moons have long memories. Better to dance badly than not at all. This one has seen Imperials dance. It is very bad. The moons forgave them anyway.

notes.title: Ri'jasha's Plea, Nailed to a Market Post
notes.author: Ri'jasha the Caravaneer
pages:
To the brave, the foolish, and the well-paid:
This one's caravan of the clan Ra'zhan stopped for water at the Peryite stones north of the city. The water was clean. The air was not. By morning her cousins were coughing, and by evening they were walking in rows around the dragon-statue, counting.

This one ran. This one is ashamed. The clan's caravan bell is still on the lead wagon, and without it the clan cannot be called home, for the bell is how the Ra'zhan call their dead to the Lattice. Find Ri'jasha in the market of Torval. She will pay with everything she has left, which is not much, and with her gratitude, which is a great deal.

senchal.hook: A great port city on Elsweyr's southern coast, home to smugglers, skooma dens and the thieves who claim descent from Rajhin himself, ringed by shrines to the Princes of shadow, secrets and nightmares.
senchal.rumour: Senchal is the finest city in Elsweyr for buying anything at all, especially things you should not. Somebody robbed the Nocturnal stones west of town. The thieves of Senchal are scandalised.

notes.title: Letter of the Rajhin's Kin
notes.author: Old Ja'khirr, called the Last Footpad
pages:
To the thieves of Senchal, all of you, even the bad ones:
Someone has robbed the Lady's stones west of the city. A gang that calls itself the Shadow-Claws. They took the offerings: coins, rings, and the bow that Rajhin himself hung at the Lady's feet, which no thief has touched in four hundred years.

A thief who robs a thief is a thief. A thief who robs the Lady is a fool, and a fool who robs Rajhin is a corpse who hasn't heard yet. This one is too old to hunt them. This one has left a message at the shrine for whoever comes next. Honour among thieves is a lie told by guardsmen. Honour toward the Lady is not.

notes.title: Harbour Ledger of Dar'jazad
notes.author: Dar'jazad
pages:
#Ships out, Last Seed
The Swift Gull for Anvil: 4 crates herbs (medicinal). Very medicinal. Very many herbs.
The Laughing Kettle for Lilmoth: 60 barrels sugar. Note: last time the Lilmoth harbour sang for three days. The Argonian King sent a polite letter. Do not send so many barrels this time.

#Payments
Thalmor customs post: the usual. Customs post (after the Renrijra Krin visited): nothing, as there is no customs post this week.
To the dream-woman at the Vaermina stones: nothing. This one does not pay that one. This one does not sleep near that one. This one recommends everybody else does the same.

shrine_azura_elsweyr.hook: A gentle statue of Azurah, mother of the Khajiit, in the dunes south-west of Rimmen, where grandmothers bring newborn cubs to be shown to the moons.
shrine_azura_elsweyr.rumour: Our grandmothers carry every new cub out to Azurah's statue south-west of Rimmen and hold it up to the moons. She made us, after all. It is only polite to show her what she made.

notes.title: A Grandmother's Prayer at the Moon-Showing
notes.author: Grandmother Za'ira of Rimmen
pages: Azurah, who shaped us from the old forest folk and gave us the moons to walk by, here is another. Her name is Ri'shara. She came on the night Masser was full and Secunda was thin, so she will be quick and stubborn, like her mother, like her grandmother, like you.

This one asks you to watch her when the Elves come to count us. This one asks you to keep her paws on the sand and her nose out of the skooma dens. This one asks you to let her be a Khajiit, whatever that means by the time she is grown. Look at her. Is she not perfect? Of course she is. You made her.

shrine_boethiah_elsweyr.hook: A warrior-statue of Boethra, the Clever Warrior, in the hills of Pellitine south of Riverhold, held by a duellist named Hazadir who has killed nine challengers in the Prince's name.
shrine_boethiah_elsweyr.rumour: Hazadir the Unbowed holds Boethra's stones in Pellitine. Nine have challenged him and nine have died, all after tea. You'd think one of them would have refused the tea.

notes.title: Letter of a Pellitine Sword-Master
notes.author: Master Ahzirr of the Silk-Blade School
pages:
To whoever stands at Boethra's stones, from Master Ahzirr:
Hazadir was my student. He was the finest and the worst. He has killed nine challengers here, my students among them, and each one drank his tea first. I have tasted the dregs. Cobweb root. A little numbness in the paw, nothing a fighter would notice until the third pass.

The Clever Warrior admires a trick. So do I. But a trick is a feint, not a poison in a cup. Challenge him. Refuse the tea. Kill him, if you can, and bring me his notched ring at Riverhold, where I teach now by the Mane's gate, so that I can take the nine notches off it one by one and say each name. Boethra will not mind. Boethra respects the one who sees the trick coming.

shrine_clavicus_vile_elsweyr.hook: A statue of Clavicus Vile in the dunes just north of Torval, where Khajiit merchants come to make the most carefully worded wishes in all of Tamriel.
shrine_clavicus_vile_elsweyr.rumour: Khajiit merchants wish at the Clavicus stones north of Torval. They bring a lawyer. Several, sometimes. The Prince, they say, enjoys it very much. Nobody else does.

notes.title: A Merchant's Wish, Drafted Seven Times
notes.author: Bazrag-dar, caravan-master
pages: Draft the seventh: This one, Bazrag-dar, of the clan of the Long Road, wishes that his caravans will reach their destinations safely (meaning with all wagons, all goods, all kin and all animals alive, whole and in their right minds), in a reasonable time (meaning not more than ten days late), without loss (meaning neither by theft, nor by fire, nor by tax, nor by Thalmor).

Note from the Prince, written in the sand after: 'Granted. And for wasting my evening with a contract, I have made you honest. Enjoy your wagons.'
Note from Bazrag-dar, a month later: 'This one cannot lie about the price of anything. This one is ruined. Never wish carefully. He hates it.'

shrine_hermaeus_mora_elsweyr.hook: A writhing statue of Herma-Mora, the Woodland Man, in the hills north of Senchal, which the Moon-Priests warn the young to avoid, for he once tried to make the Khajiit his own.
shrine_hermaeus_mora_elsweyr.rumour: The Moon-Priests tell cubs about the Woodland Man in the hills north of Senchal. He tried to steal the Khajiit away from Azurah once, long ago. They say he is still waiting for someone curious enough.

notes.title: A Moon-Priest's Warning
notes.author: Moon-Priest Talizar of Senchal
pages: Cub, if you have walked this far to the Woodland Man's stones, you are curious. Curiosity is a fine thing in a Khajiit. It is how we find the best fish. But listen to this one now.

Herma-Mora once whispered to the Khajiit that they need not be Azurah's children; that they could be his, and know everything, and stop being cats. Some listened. Alkosh and the Riddle'Thar brought them home, but they came back with something missing behind the eyes.
Turn round. Go home. Ask your grandmother the question you came here to ask. She will not know the answer. She will give you a fish. That is better.

shrine_hircine_elsweyr.hook: A beast-headed statue of Hircine in the scrubland west of Rimmen, where the hunters of the city ask the Huntsman for a fair chase against the great senche-tigers of the plains.
shrine_hircine_elsweyr.rumour: Rimmen's hunters ask the Huntsman for a fair chase against the senche-tigers. A fair chase against a senche is when you run and it doesn't catch you. This one doesn't hunt.

notes.title: Hunt Journal of Do'zakha
notes.author: Do'zakha, hunter of Rimmen
pages:
#First day
Asked the Huntsman for a great senche. Left him a jerky. This one thinks the Huntsman does not like jerky. This one thinks perhaps a better offering would have been wise.

#Second day
Found the great senche. It found this one first. We looked at each other for a long time. Then it lay down and yawned and let a cub out from behind it, a little one, very fierce, who tried to eat this one's boot.
#Third day
The cub has followed this one home. This one will raise it. The Huntsman has a sense of humour. Next time this one will bring a better offering. Next time this one will also bring more boots.

shrine_malacath_elsweyr.hook: A statue of Malooc, the Orcs' god and old enemy of the Khajiit, in the hills south of Riverhold, kept by Orc caravan guards whom the Khajiit hire, distrust, and quietly need.
shrine_malacath_elsweyr.rumour: The Orc caravan guards keep the Malooc stones south of Riverhold. Malooc is the Khajiit's old enemy. The Orcs know. They pray there anyway, loudly, just so we hear.

notes.title: Oath Cut by Orc Caravan Guards
notes.author: Gashna gra-Shug and the Iron Road guards
pages: Malacath, Malooc, whatever the cats call you, it is your name. Your sons and daughters guard Khajiit wagons on the sand roads. The cats pay us. They don't thank us. They tell their cubs stories about you with us standing right there.

We swear: we will guard the wagons. We will take the arrows. We will not take the moon sugar, even though it is right there, and it smells good. When the Renrijra Krin come laughing, we will stand. When the cats tell their stories, we will laugh louder. One day a cat will thank us. On that day we will carve the name here, so you can see it too.

shrine_mehrunes_dagon_elsweyr.hook: A jagged statue of Merrunz, the cat-demon who is Mehrunes Dagon to the Khajiit, in the dunes north-east of Torval, where Moon-Priests come to bind the fires that leap from its eyes on moonless nights.
shrine_mehrunes_dagon_elsweyr.rumour: The Merrunz stones north-east of Torval spit fire from their eyes when there's no moon. The Moon-Priests go out with water and songs. So far the songs have worked. So far.

notes.title: Record of a Binding
notes.author: Moon-Priest Ahnissi
pages: On the third moonless night of Frostfall, the eyes of Merrunz took fire again. Three priests went with the songs of binding and the water of the Torval wells. The flames sang back. They sang the Riddle'Thar backwards, which this one has never heard before and wishes not to hear again.

We bound them by dawn. Priest Jo'zarra's whiskers burned off and will not grow back. She says she does not mind; she says she is lighter now. This one asks the Bishop to send five priests next time, not three. Merrunz is learning the songs. A demon who learns is a demon who waits.

shrine_mephala_elsweyr.hook: A spider-limbed statue of Mafala in the hills west of Senchal, where the Clan Mothers of the southern coast keep the secret rites that Mafala taught their ancestors.
shrine_mephala_elsweyr.rumour: The Clan Mothers go to Mafala's stones west of Senchal and come back knowing everything about everyone. That is not a rumour. That is how being a Clan Mother works.

notes.title: Letter Between Clan Mothers
notes.author: Clan Mother Shazzira of Senchal
pages:
Sister Nazhira,
This one went to Mafala's stones on the dark of Secunda. The Weaver showed this one the threads of the Senchal clans. Your nephew is stealing from the harbour. My grandson is stealing from your nephew. The harbour master is stealing from both. Nobody is stealing from the Thalmor, which is a disgrace.

This one proposes the usual: we say nothing to the men, we arrange two marriages, we let the harbour master keep his post and his life in exchange for a tenth. Mafala taught our grandmothers that every secret is a thread. Pull gently. Never cut. Tie, and keep the knots where only we can see.

shrine_meridia_elsweyr.hook: A shining statue of Meridia on the border hills north of Rimmen, where a stubborn Imperial pilgrim from Bravil has lived for years, burning the walking dead of the old war out of the dunes.
shrine_meridia_elsweyr.rumour: There's an old Imperial woman at the Meridia stones north of Rimmen. She came from Bravil to burn the dead. Elsweyr has a great deal of dead. She is very busy.

notes.title: Letter Home to Bravil
notes.author: Sister Gratia Vell
pages:
Dear Marcella,
Yes, I am still alive. No, I am not coming home. The dunes north of Rimmen are thick with the dead of the old wars, Imperial and Khajiit both, and some necromancer in the Void Nights stirred them up and never laid them down again. The Lady's light is the only thing they fear.

The Khajiit think I am mad. They bring me dates and leave quickly. One of them, a little Cathay boy, asked me why I don't go home. I told him: because I finally found something I'm good at. He thought about it and said 'this one is good at stealing dates'. We have an arrangement now.

shrine_molag_bal_elsweyr.hook: A hulking statue of Molag Bal in the hills just south of Riverhold, where slavers have begun to gather Khajiit captives, almost in sight of the Mane's own walls.
shrine_molag_bal_elsweyr.rumour: Slavers at the Molag Bal stones south of Riverhold, they say. The Mane's guard says they're rumours. The Mane's guard also sent two riders to look. The riders haven't come back.

notes.title: Ra'vinni's Report, Unfinished
notes.author: Ra'vinni of the Mane's Guard
pages: Captain, this one is writing in the rocks above the stones. Do'sara is watching. The rumours are true. Twelve captives, Khajiit, chained to the Lord of Brutality's statue, with a Bosmer and two Imperials standing guard and a fourth person who wears no colours at all.

The fourth person carries a paper with a Thalmor seal. This one cannot see the words. Do'sara says do not fight. This one is a Cathay-raht and wishes to fight very much. This one will wait for the guard. If the guard does not come, this one will not wait

shrine_namira_elsweyr.hook: A statue of Namiira, the Great Darkness, in the dunes north-west of Torval, where the dark-souled Dro-m'Athra gather on moonless nights, and where a mother has gone looking for the son she lost to them.
shrine_namira_elsweyr.rumour: The Dro-m'Athra gather at Namiira's stones north-west of Torval when there are no moons. Old Za'mira's son J'kar went out there to steal from them. He came back, in a way. He came back wrong.

notes.title: A Mother's Letter, Left at the Stones
notes.author: Za'mira of Torval
pages:
J'kar, my cub,
You came to these stones to steal a dark-moon pendant from the Dro-m'Athra, because a fool in a skooma den said it would bring you luck. You stole it. You put it on. And when you came home, your shadow did not come with you.

Now you walk with them on the moonless nights. You looked at me last time through the window and there was nothing behind your eyes. The Moon-Priests say the pendant holds you to Namiira. Whoever reads this: break my son's hold. Take the pendant. If you have to end him to do it, then end him gently, and bring the pendant out into the light. He was a good boy. He was a very bad thief.

shrine_nocturnal_elsweyr.hook: A hooded statue of Nocturnal in the hills north-west of Senchal, sacred to the city's thieves, robbed this season of its offerings, including a bow hung there by Rajhin the Footpad himself.
shrine_nocturnal_elsweyr.rumour: The Shadow-Claws robbed the Lady's stones near Senchal. Took Rajhin's own bow, they say. Every thief in Senchal wants them dead. Not one of them dares to do it. Funny how that works.

notes.title: The Last Footpad's Message
notes.author: Old Ja'khirr, called the Last Footpad
pages: If you are reading this, you are standing where Rajhin stood. He hung his bow at the Lady's feet four hundred years ago and swore never to steal again. Then he stole the oath back. That is the story. Nobody knows if it is true.

The Shadow-Claws took it. Their chief is Jo'vahn, called the Unlucky, and he is about to be very much more unlucky. They have a hideout in the rocks close by, and they come back to the stones to mock the Lady with her own offerings. Find them. Take back the offering box. Rajhin's bow is the Lady's to give, not theirs to keep. The Lady may decide you have earned it. Rajhin would have.

shrine_peryite_elsweyr.hook: A dragon-shaped statue of Peryite in the dunes north of Torval, beside a clear spring, where Ri'jasha's caravan stopped for water and her clan caught the Taskmaster's orderly plague.
shrine_peryite_elsweyr.rumour: Don't drink at the Peryite spring north of Torval. Ri'jasha's clan did. They're still out there, walking in rows around the statue, counting. Counting what, nobody wants to know.

notes.title: A List Scratched on a Wagon Board
notes.author: one of the clan Ra'zhan
pages: One. Two. Three wagons. Four wheels. Sixteen wheels. Thirty-two spokes. Spokes are in order. Wagons are in order. Cousins are in order. Cousin Ri'jasha is not in order. Cousin Ri'jasha ran.

The Taskmaster says that is a mistake. The Taskmaster says mistakes are corrected. The bell on the lead wagon rings out of order when the wind blows. The bell must be stopped. The bell is the last thing that is out of order.
One. Two. Three. This one cannot remember what this one was before this one could count. This one does not mind. Four.

shrine_sanguine_elsweyr.hook: A grinning statue of Sanguine in the hills west of Riverhold, where moon-sugar revels last for days and the Mane's own cooks have been known to leave the soup to join them.
shrine_sanguine_elsweyr.rumour: The Sanguine stones west of Riverhold have a revel every full moon. Sugar, wine, music. The Mane's cooks keep slipping out to join it. This one has tasted the Mane's soup lately and does not blame them.

notes.title: The Cook's Confession
notes.author: Ma'jhad, under-cook to the Mane
pages:
Captain Shazar-ri,
You asked why the cooks keep going to the Sanguine stones. Here is the truth. The Prince's revellers have a spice. It is not moon sugar. It is not skooma. It is a red powder that makes a stew taste like your grandmother's on the best day she ever had.

We go to get the spice. We stay for the dancing. We come back without our aprons, sometimes without our names, but always with the spice. The Mane has never eaten so well. If the Mane asks, it is a family recipe. It is, in a way. The Prince says he is everyone's family, at a revel.

shrine_sheogorath_elsweyr.hook: A grinning statue of Sheggorath, the Skooma Cat, in the dunes just east of Torval, where addicts come to bargain for one more dream and Moon-Priests come to bargain them back.
shrine_sheogorath_elsweyr.rumour: The Skooma Cat's stones east of Torval are full of dreamers and the Moon-Priests who chase them. Sheggorath laughs at both. This one has heard him. He sounds like a kettle.

notes.title: Riddle of the Skooma Cat
notes.author: carved by a dreamer
pages:
~What is the cat who is sweet and who bites?
~What is the moon that is three moons at night?
~What is the dream that you buy and you lose?
~And what is the Lattice when no one can choose?

Beneath, in a Moon-Priest's tidy hand: 'The answers are skooma, skooma, skooma and skooma. Go home.'
Beneath that, scratched: 'Wrong. The answer is cheese. The Skooma Cat says so. He also says the Moon-Priest has a crumb in her whiskers, and she does, this one checked, and now this one believes everything.'

shrine_vaermina_elsweyr.hook: A dark statue of Vaermina in the hills south-west of Senchal, where a dream-woman sells nightmares to skooma-sleepers, and no honest smuggler in the city will sleep within a mile of her.
shrine_vaermina_elsweyr.rumour: There's a dream-woman at the Vaermina stones south-west of Senchal. Even Dar'jazad won't deal with her, and Dar'jazad deals with Thalmor. That should tell you enough.

notes.title: Warning Scratched on a Smuggler's Crate
notes.author: a smuggler of Senchal
pages:
Do not sleep here. Do not sleep here. Do not sleep here.
This one slept here, one night, after too much sugar, by the statue, because the ground was warm. This one dreamed of the Void Nights, when the moons were gone, every night of two years, in one night.

When this one woke, the dream-woman was sitting by this one's head with a little glass jar, and she said 'thank you, that one will sell very well in Bravil'. This one has not dreamed since. Not one dream. Not a good one, not a bad one. That is worse than you would think. Do not sleep here.
